docs.text:
/// Wall-clock instant; serializes as RFC 3339 UTC with millisecond precision.
pub struct Timestamp(SystemTime);

#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct HostInfo {
    pub os: String,              // std::env::consts::OS
    pub arch: String,            // std::env::consts::ARCH
    pub hostname: String,        // HOSTNAME / COMPUTERNAME env var, or "unknown"
    pub mallops_version: String, // CARGO_PKG_VERSION
}

#[non_exhaustive]
#[serde(tag = "event", rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum LineageEvent {
    #[non_exhaustive]
    RunStarted {
        run: RunId,
        timestamp: Timestamp,
        pipeline_hash: Digest,
        git_commit: Option<String>,
        host: HostInfo,
    },
    #[non_exhaustive]
    BlockStarted {
        run: RunId,
        timestamp: Timestamp,
        node: String,
        block: BlockRef,         // serialized via Display as a string (e.g. "std/external")
        block_version: String,
        config_hash: Digest,
        seed: Option<u64>,
        inputs: Vec<ArtifactId>,
    },
    #[non_exhaustive]
    ArtifactProduced { run: RunId, timestamp: Timestamp, node: String, artifact: ArtifactId },
    #[non_exhaustive]
    BlockFinished {
        run: RunId,
        timestamp: Timestamp,
        node: String,
        status: Status,          // snake_case: succeeded | failed | skipped | cancelled
        duration: Duration,      // serialized as `duration_ms: u64`
        cached: bool,
    },
    #[non_exhaustive]
    RunFinished { run: RunId, timestamp: Timestamp, status: Status },
}

pub trait LineageSink: Send + Sync {
    fn record<'a>(&'a self, event: &'a LineageEvent) -> BoxFuture<'a, Result<(), Error>>;
}
  • The runtime is the only producer: it alone sees the whole graph. Blocks stay unaware of lineage.
  • Document format (JsonSink): writes runs/<run-id>/lineage.json through ArtifactStore::put_meta (on LocalStore: meta/runs/<run-id>/lineage.json) as {"v":1,"run":"<run-id>","events":[...]}. Events use an internally tagged snake_case "event" field (run_started, block_started, artifact_produced, block_finished, run_finished); timestamp is RFC 3339 UTC with millisecond precision (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.mmmZ, computed from UNIX_EPOCH without an external date crate); BlockStarted.block serializes as a string; BlockFinished.duration serializes as duration_ms (u64); Status serializes in snake_case. JsonSink buffers events per run and rewrites the file on every event so it remains valid JSON after a crash, freeing the run's buffer on RunFinished.
  • Configuration (RuntimeConfig): lineage defaults to [JsonSink::new(store)] (empty Vec disables lineage, corresponding to lineage: off; mallops-cli maps off → vec![] and sink: json → JsonSink::new(store), rejecting unknown sinks in validate, run, and store verify), clock defaults to SystemTime::now (injectable for deterministic tests), host defaults to HostInfo::current() (reads HOSTNAME, falling back to COMPUTERNAME or "unknown" — env-only, no unsafe/libc), and git_commit defaults to None in the core library (mallops run populates it via best-effort git rev-parse HEAD in the directory of mallops.yaml with stderr suppressed; never spawned by validate, graph, or store verify).
  • pipeline_hash: blake3::derive_key("mallops pipeline v1", ...) over the canonical JSON array of validated nodes in topological order (id, use, BlockSpec.version, config_hash, in, seed).
  • Event order and statuses:
  • Started node: BlockStarted → one ArtifactProduced per output in NodeSummary.outputs → BlockFinished. Cache hits still emit BlockStarted, ArtifactProduced for every cached output, and BlockFinished with cached: true.
  • Node that never starts (stopped by gate, cancelled before starting, or unscheduled): only BlockFinished with duration_ms: 0 and cached: false.
  • Panicking node task: BlockStarted (already emitted) followed by BlockFinished (status: "failed", duration_ms: 0, cached: false).
  • RunFinished.status: Cancelled if RuntimeConfig::cancel fired, else Succeeded if RunSummary::is_success(), else Failed.
  • Dispatch and fault isolation: every event is sent to each sink in RuntimeConfig::lineage in order; if a sink returns Err, the runtime logs tracing::warn! and continues to the remaining sinks — a failing sink never fails the run.
  • Conformance suite: mallops_core::lineage::conformance::check_sink verifies a full event sequence covering all four Status variants and interleaved concurrent runs (supporting both read-back and write-only sinks), reusable by future sink backends (SQLite, OpenLineage, MLflow — mallops-std features or plugins in v0.2+).
  • Caching does not depend on lineage: it uses artifact hashes and cache/<key>.json in the store.

docs.title: 7. Serving
docs.text:
Serving runs outside the batch DAG via mallops serve [package-id] (using the package artifact produced by mallops run or configured in the top-level serve: section of mallops.yaml). Transports: HTTP (v0.1), gRPC (v0.2) and MQTT (v0.3, serve.transport: mqtt: request topic in, prediction topic out, see ADR-0009).

flowchart LR
    C[Client] -->|HTTP/gRPC/MQTT| S[mallops serve]
    S --> T[Preprocess transform<br/>from package]
    T --> P{Predictor by flavor}
    P --> SC[smartcore]
    P --> O[ort]
    P --> TR[tract]
    P --> CA[candle]
    P --> EXT[external Python worker]
    S --> M[metrics / logs]

In v0.1, the minimal Predictor contract lives in mallops-std (shared by evaluate and serve) before promotion to mallops-core ahead of 1.0 (ADR-0007):

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum PredictInput {
    Json(serde_json::Value),
    Bytes { content_type: String, data: Vec<u8> },
}

pub trait Predictor: Send + Sync {
    fn flavors(&self) -> &[&str];
    fn executes_code(&self) -> bool;
    fn load<'a>(
        &'a self,
        artifact: &'a Artifact,
        payload_dir: &'a Path,
    ) -> BoxFuture<'a, Result<Box<dyn LoadedPredictor>, Error>>;
}

pub trait LoadedPredictor: Send + Sync {
    fn predict(&self, input: PredictInput) -> BoxFuture<'_, Result<PredictInput, Error>>;
    fn predict_batch(
        &self,
        inputs: Vec<PredictInput>,
    ) -> BoxFuture<'_, Result<Vec<PredictInput>, Error>>;
}

Consumers resolve a predictor through PredictorRegistry, which registers predictors by flavor atomically and enforces trust policy: flavors where executes_code() is true (such as sklearn-pickle) are rejected by PredictorRegistry::get with Error::Config unless trust_unsafe_flavors is explicitly passed (CLI: --trust-unsafe-flavors). See the full Predictor contract reference.

Behind the serve-http feature, mallops-std provides mallops_std::serve (ServeOptions, Server, ServeHandle) over axum (HTTP/1.1):

  • Request flow: GET /health bypasses auth, timeout, and concurrency limits so probes stay responsive under load. POST /predict passes through metadata-only logging → timeout (504) → optional constant-time BLAKE3 bearer auth (401, before body read) → semaphore concurrency permit (503) → body size limit (413) → JSON decode → optional FittedTransform::apply_json → LoadedPredictor.
  • Zero-downtime hot-swap: Server::handle() yields a Clone ServeHandle with async fn swap(store, id, predictors) -> Result<bool, Error>. Swaps are serialized with an async mutex; the replacement state (Package::load in a fresh tempdir, trust-gate check, transform, and Predictor::load) is built completely before atomically replacing the Arc<State> behind a RwLock (never held across .await). In-flight requests finish on the previous Arc<State>, dropping the old predictor and tempdir only after the last request completes; any load or trust error logs a tracing warn and keeps the active package untouched. mallops-std stays signal-agnostic: on Unix, mallops-cli installs a SIGHUP handler before initial load, re-reads runs/latest.json, and calls ServeHandle::swap (ignoring SIGHUP with a warning: ... line on stderr when an explicit PACKAGE_ID was given; the CLI does not depend on tracing). See the mallops serve reference.

docs.title: 8. Edge and federated learning (v0.4)
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    subgraph Cloud
        AGG[FL aggregator]
        REGI[Model registry]
        COL[Metrics collector]
    end
    subgraph Edge["Edge node (mallops-edge)"]
        SV[Local serving HTTP/MQTT]
        OL[Online learning DAG]
        LT[FL local training]
        BUF[Metrics buffer]
    end
    REGI -- signed model pull --> SV
    AGG -- global weights --> LT
    LT -- weight deltas only --> AGG
    SEN[Sensor] -- MQTT readings --> SV -- MQTT predictions --> CON[Consumer]
    SEN -- labelled samples --> OL -- new package if gate passes --> SV
    SV --> BUF -- push when online --> COL
    COL -- drift alert --> RT[Retrain trigger]
  • Transport: gRPC (tonic) with mTLS for the fleet control plane and FL; nodes initiate connections (NAT-friendly). MQTT for device data: serving reads requests from a topic and publishes predictions (ADR-0009).
  • Build: mallops-edge is inference-only by default (profile-edge); online and fl add only the training backends they need (ADR-0008).
  • Online learning: a finite DAG on the device produces a new immutable package from the current model (base input of incremental train blocks); serving hot-swaps only after the evaluate gate passes, keeps the previous accepted and base packages for rollback, and never mutates a served model.
  • Aggregation strategies are blocks (FedAvg default); privacy techniques plug in at the aggregator.
  • Model weights exchanged in whatever format the flavor defines; the aggregator delegates averaging to a flavor-aware plugin.

docs.title: 9. Cross-cutting concerns
docs.text: Concern Choice Errors thiserror in libraries (mallops_core::Error), anyhow only in the CLI Logging/tracing tracing (tracing-subscriber fmt on stderr in mallops-cli: WARN default, DEBUG with -v/--verbose); OpenTelemetry exporter behind a feature Config serde + serde_json + yaml_serde (yaml feature, enabled by default) + optional schemars (schema feature); ${env:NAME} interpolated at load time in with/store.path only, ${secret:NAME} stays symbolic Async tokio (rt-multi-thread and signal in mallops-cli) CLI clap derive (exit codes: 0 success, 1 error, 2 usage error) Testing unit tests per crate, integration tests running example pipelines, insta snapshots for CLI output

docs.title: mallops — Technical Specification
docs.text: Status: Draft · Target: v0.1 · Last update: 2026-11-27

docs.title: 1. Vision
docs.text:
mallops is a modular MLOps framework written in Rust. It covers the whole machine-learning lifecycle — from data ingestion to serving, monitoring and retraining, down to edge devices with federated learning — through composable blocks.

It can be used in three ways, all backed by the same core:

Mode Who How Library Rust developers depend on mallops-core, implement Block, compose pipelines in code Plugins anyone, any language ship a block as a WASM component or as an external process speaking the mallops gRPC protocol Standalone ML engineers, ops describe a pipeline in mallops.yaml, run it with the mallops CLI, add/remove blocks without writing code

docs.title: 1.1 Design principles
docs.text:
1. Format and library agnostic. mallops never imposes a model format, a data format or an ML library. An artifact is opaque files + a manifest. ONNX, safetensors, TorchScript, pickle, GGUF, XGBoost JSON, a custom binary — all first-class.
  2. Everything is a block. Every lifecycle step, including data storage, deploy and retrain triggers, is a replaceable block with declared inputs and outputs (artifact store and lineage are core contracts acting on every edge; see ADR-0006).
  3. Small core, optional everything else. The core has no ML dependency. Standard blocks live behind Cargo feature flags.
  4. Reproducible by default. Content-addressed artifacts, recorded configs, seeds and environment.
  5. Local first, scale out later. A full pipeline runs on a laptop with zero infrastructure; the same pipeline targets object storage, remote runners and edge fleets by swapping blocks.

docs.title: 1.2 Non-goals
docs.text:
• Not a container orchestrator (it can call Kubernetes, Nomad, Docker as deploy blocks).
  • Not a deep-learning framework (it wraps burn, candle, PyTorch, scikit-learn, …).
  • Not a data warehouse or feature store (it integrates with them via blocks).
  • No GUI in v1 (a dashboard may come as a separate project).

docs.title: 2. Glossary
docs.text: Term Definition Block Unit of work with typed inputs, outputs and config. Implements the Block trait (or the plugin protocol). Stage Lifecycle category a block belongs to (ingest, preprocess, train, …). Used for docs, validation hints and CLI listing — not enforced ordering. Artifact Immutable output of a block: a set of files plus a manifest, identified by its content hash. Pipeline DAG of block instances wired by artifact references, defined in YAML or code. Run One execution of a pipeline; has an id, a lineage record and logs. Flavor Tag in a model manifest telling which loader/predictor can use it (e.g. onnx, torchscript, sklearn-pickle, gguf, custom:acme). Artifact store Internal storage through which blocks exchange artifacts. Contract in the core, backends pluggable. Not to be confused with data storage blocks. Lineage sink Pluggable destination of the lineage events emitted by the runtime (JSON file, SQLite, OpenLineage, MLflow…). Plugin Block distributed outside the mallops binary (Rust crate, WASM component, or external process). Edge node Device running mallops-edge: local serving, local metrics, optional federated training.

docs.title: 3. Functional requirements
docs.text: Each stage below lists what the standard library of blocks (mallops-std) must offer and what the core must make possible. Anything not covered can be added as a plugin.

docs.title: 3.1 Data ingestion
docs.text:
• FR-ING-1: read from local files — in v0.1, mallops-std provides std/ingest.csv (feature ingest-csv) and std/ingest.parquet (feature ingest-parquet; meta-feature ingest, enabled by default), both Stage::Ingest version 0.1.0; JSON/NDJSON and arbitrary-file ingest blocks are deferred follow-ups:
  • Both blocks reject unknown with: keys (deny_unknown_fields), run file I/O, conversion, and source hashing on tokio::task::spawn_blocking (checking ctx.cancel() between batches), resolve relative path values against the current working directory (mallops run changes into the directory of mallops.yaml, matching store.path), emit one dataset output (kind: dataset, format: parquet) backed by a single uncompressed data.parquet file with fixed footer created_by: "mallops-std" (deterministic bytes per mallops-std version) committed by the runtime (never calling store.put directly), and return CachePolicy::Deterministic { extra_hash: Some(blake3(source_file)) } (streamed BLAKE3 digest; missing source file errors) so editing the local file invalidates cached runs. Known v0.1 limitation: extra_hash is computed in cache_policy and the file is read again in run (TOCTOU); modifying a local source file concurrently during a run can associate the old cache key with the new content.
  • std/ingest.csv with: config: path (required), delimiter (ASCII char other than \n, \r, or ", default ','; invalid values fail with Error::Config), has_header (bool, default true), schema (optional list of { name, type }). Empty CSV files (0 columns) fail with empty CSV: no columns; header-only files (0 data rows) are valid. Without schema, column types are inferred across the entire file (arrow-csv may also infer Null for all-empty columns or Timestamp for ISO-8601 datetime strings — second-precision timestamps are promoted to milliseconds because Parquet has no seconds unit, so non-Arrow readers such as pandas see a timestamp rather than an integer — which lie outside the v0.1 schema: subset and therefore cannot be validated with schema: — a known v0.1 limitation). With schema, has_header: true requires the CSV header to match the declared column names in exact order (schema mismatch otherwise), while has_header: false checks that the first row has the exact declared column count (schema mismatch: expected N columns, found M) and assigns the declared names. Empty cells parse as null; non-empty unconvertible values fail the node with an error naming the source file.
  • std/ingest.parquet with: config: path (required), schema (optional list of { name, type }). Reads external Parquet files compressed with Snappy, LZ4, Gzip, or Zstd (as well as uncompressed), checks exact column names and types in order when schema is set (schema mismatch otherwise), strips source schema and field key-value metadata (e.g. pandas), and rewrites an uncompressed data.parquet so identical data with different source metadata produces identical bytes.
  • FR-ING-2: read from HTTP(S) and object stores (S3, GCS, Azure) — v0.2.
  • FR-ING-3: read from databases (PostgreSQL, SQLite) and streams (Kafka, MQTT) — v0.3+. MQTT: std/ingest.mqtt, a bounded read (max_messages, max_duration or idle_timeout) into a dataset, uncacheable, at-least-once up to the block return (ADR-0009).
  • FR-ING-4: optional schema validation accepts the v0.1 column type subset bool | int64 | float64 | string | date32 (Arrow Boolean, Int64, Float64, Utf8, Date32; nullability ignored), checked as header names (or column count when has_header: false) plus typed parsing for std/ingest.csv and exact column names and types in order for std/ingest.parquet; incremental ingestion is deferred to sources that support it.

docs.title: 3.2 Data storage
docs.text:
Two distinct concerns, deliberately kept apart (ADR-0006):

a) Data storage blocks — persisting user data to external systems is an ordinary, optional stage. - FR-STO-1: blocks that write datasets/features to object stores, data lakes (Delta, Iceberg), databases and feature stores — v0.2+; std/storage.mqtt publishes artifacts to MQTT topics — v0.3 (ADR-0009).

b) Artifact store — the internal mechanism through which blocks hand artifacts to each other. Not a block: it sits on every edge of the DAG. - FR-STO-2: the core defines the immutable ArtifactStore contract (plus an auxiliary metadata API for cache entries, run lineage records, and future registry entries) and ships two minimal implementations: local (filesystem, default) and memory (ephemeral, for tests and throwaway runs) — v0.1 (ADR-0007). - FR-STO-3: remote backends (S3, GCS, Azure, …) are optional (mallops-std features or plugins) — v0.2. - FR-STO-4: content addressing (canonical BLAKE3 over manifest and payload, excluding run provenance) — identical content is stored once; enables caching and resume. - FR-STO-5: garbage collection of artifacts unreachable from retained runs — v0.2.

docs.title: 3.3 Preprocessing (data → features)
docs.text:
• FR-PRE-1: tabular transforms on Arrow data — in v0.1, mallops-std provides std/preprocess.tabular (feature preprocess-tabular, enabled by default, Stage::Preprocess, version 0.1.0):
  • Ports: input data (kind: dataset, format: parquet); outputs train and test (kind: features, format: parquet), transform (kind: transform, format: json), plus optional validation (kind: features, format: parquet), resolved via Block::resolve_ports if and only if split.validation is configured (wiring features.validation without split.validation fails mallops validate at blocks.<id>.in.<port>).
  • Execution & caching: runs in tokio::task::spawn_blocking with ctx.cancel() checks, uses CachePolicy::Deterministic { extra_hash: None }, writes uncompressed data.parquet partitions (created_by: "mallops-std") with metadata["target"] and io_schema = { "features": [{ "name", "type" }], "target": { "name", "type" } }, and writes the fitted transform to transform.json. Known v0.1 limitation: the entire input Parquet dataset is loaded into memory for splitting and transforming.
  • with: config (deny_unknown_fields): target (non-empty column name; must exist in the input dataset, is never transformed, is always preserved by select, and is recorded in metadata["target"]) and steps (ordered list of - <step>: { … }).
  • Step ordering (leakage prevention): split must appear exactly once. Stateless steps (select, filter) may appear before or after split; stateful/fitted steps (impute, scale, encode) are only allowed after split so parameters are fitted on the train partition alone and then applied to train, validation (if configured), and test.
  • Supported column types: at split (and in the final output), every remaining column must be in the v0.1 subset bool | int64 | float64 | string | date32; unsupported Arrow types fail with Error::Runtime (suggesting a select step before split for non-target columns; dedicated error without suggesting select for target).
  • Step semantics:
    • select: { columns: [...] } (non-empty, unique — validated by validate_config / mallops validate): keeps the listed columns in order plus target appended if not already listed (target is optional when replaying at serving time).
    • filter: { column, op, value? }: keeps rows matching op (eq | ne | lt | le | gt | ge with value: number on int64/float64, string on utf8, bool on boolean; is_null | not_null with value forbidden). Null values never satisfy a comparison; incompatible types fail with Error::Runtime. When filter appears after split, non-emptiness of train, test, and any configured validation is re-checked (an empty partition fails with Error::Runtime). filter only shapes batch partitions and is not replayed at serving time.
    • split: { test, validation?, seed }: test and optional validation in (0, 1) with test + validation < 1. Deterministic internal SplitMix64 PRNG + Fisher-Yates shuffle (no external RNG crate): partition sizes are computed deterministically via floor(n * ratio) in IEEE-754 f64; the first floor(n * test) indices go to test, the next floor(n * validation) (if configured) to validation, and the remainder to train; placing test first keeps test identical when validation is toggled with the same seed. Each partition preserves original relative row order (sorted indices). An empty dataset or any empty requested partition fails with Error::Runtime.
    • impute: { strategy: mean | median | constant, value?, columns? }: value (number or string) is required for constant and forbidden for mean/median. Default columns are numeric (int64, float64) non-target for mean/median and numeric constant, and utf8 non-target for string constant. mean and median compute over non-null values (all-null column fails) and always output float64 even on int64 inputs (keeping the output schema independent of the data); integer constant on int64 stays int64 (float constant casts to float64), and utf8 columns take a string constant. Non-finite float values (NaN, ±inf) fail with Error::Runtime at both fit and apply.
    • scale: { method: standard | minmax, columns? }: default columns are numeric (int64, float64) non-target; standard fits offset = mean and scale = population stddev, minmax fits offset = min and scale = max - min (all-null column fails). Outputs float64 via (x - offset) / scale; scale == 0 maps valid values to 0.0; nulls remain null. Non-finite float values (NaN, ±inf) fail with Error::Runtime at both fit and apply.
    • encode: { method: ordinal | one_hot, columns? }: default columns are utf8 non-target; collects sorted unique non-null categories (BTreeSet) from train. ordinal outputs int64 category indices (-1 for unseen or null); one_hot replaces <col> in place with float64 columns <col>=<cat> in category order (all 0.0 for unseen or null) and fails with Error::Runtime if a generated <col>=<cat> name collides with an existing or another generated column.
    • Explicit columns referencing target, a missing column, or an unsupported type fail with Error::Runtime naming the column.
  • FR-PRE-2: user-defined transforms (Rust closure, WASM, external process — in v0.1 via std/external).
  • FR-PRE-3: fitted transforms are themselves artifacts (kind: transform, format: json, payload/transform.json = {"v":1,"target":…,"input":[…],"steps":[…]} serialized deterministically, io_schema = { "input": […], "output": […] } where output records the training output schema including target), capturing fitted steps (select, impute, scale, ordinal, one_hot; never filter or split). mallops_std::FittedTransform reloads the artifact (from_dir, rejecting versions other than 1) and replays it so serving applies the exact same preprocessing:
  • apply_batch: projects the incoming RecordBatch onto input columns in input order (target optional, extra columns ignored) with strict Arrow type checks (Error::Runtime naming the column, expected, and found types) before applying the fitted steps.
  • apply_json: accepts a JSON array of row objects keyed by input columns (target optional, unknown keys ignored, explicit null allowed; a missing key for a non-target column fails with Error::Runtime("…row {i}: missing column '{col}'"); int64 columns accept whole-number floats; type mismatches report row index and column name), builds the RecordBatch, and applies the exact same steps as apply_batch.
  • FR-PRE-4: data validation: check a tabular dataset against declared expectations before preprocessing or training — in v0.1, mallops-std provides std/validate.tabular (feature validate, not in default, enabled in mallops-cli; Stage::Preprocess, version 0.1.0; see std/validate.tabular):
  • Ports: required input data (kind: dataset, format: parquet); outputs data (kind: dataset, format: parquet, same payload and manifest as the input, with a new ArtifactId because the runtime sets parents to the input per ADR-0007 D3) and report (kind: metrics, format: json, report.json).
  • with: config (deny_unknown_fields, ${secret: rejected): optional schema (list of { name, type } in bool | int64 | float64 | string | date32), allow_extra_columns (default true), optional min_rows, optional per-column checks (max_null_fraction, min, max, allowed, unique), and on_fail: fail | skip (default fail, unlike FR-EVL-2's skip). Incoherent configs (min > max, max_null_fraction outside [0, 1], non-finite bounds, a column without an active check, empty or non-string/int64/bool allowed, allow_extra_columns: false without schema) fail with Error::Config.
  • Evaluation & report: all checks are evaluated and every data problem (missing column, wrong type, min/max on non-numeric column, allowed on float64) is recorded as a failed check rather than a runtime error. Nulls count only toward max_null_fraction (0 rows ⇒ null fraction 0; all-null columns pass min/max); NaN always fails min/max; allowed applies only to string/int64/bool. report.json is {"v":1,"passed":…,"checks":[{"check", "column"?, "passed", "observed", "expected"}]} in fixed deterministic order (schema, min_rows, columns alphabetically), serializing NaN/±inf as strings "NaN"/"inf"/"-inf" and reporting allowed/unique violations as count + up to 5 sorted distinct examples (unique count = occurrences beyond the first). The report manifest carries metadata.passed.
  • Gate & caching: CachePolicy::Deterministic { extra_hash: None }. On failure, on_fail: fail returns Error::Validation with one item per failed check, per offending column for schema, never carrying data values (report paths schema.<col>, min_rows, checks.<col>.<check>, not YAML paths); on_fail: skip returns BlockOutcome::Skipped (reason validation failed: <paths>; downstream nodes with required inputs are skipped, report reaches only optional inputs, mallops run leaves runs/latest.json unchanged and exits 0). Statistical drift detection is deferred to v0.3 (FR-MON-3), and streaming/out-of-core validation to v0.2 (NFR-8).

docs.title: 3.4 Training
docs.text:
• FR-TRN-1: native Rust training (smartcore for classic ML) — v0.1. The block is std/train.smartcore (feature train-smartcore, not in default; binary logistic regression and linear regression); see std/train.smartcore.
  • FR-TRN-2: deep learning via burn/candle — v0.3.
  • FR-TRN-3: external trainer: run any command/container (Python, R, Julia…) that reads input artifacts and writes outputs into a mallops-managed workspace directory — v0.1. This is how PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn, XGBoost are supported without Rust bindings. In v0.1 this is provided by the generic std/external block (CLI contract v1).
  • FR-TRN-4: hyperparameters, seed and environment recorded in the run lineage.

docs.title: 3.5 Model engineering
docs.text:
• FR-ENG-1: hyperparameter search (grid, random; Bayesian as plugin) as a block that fans out training sub-runs — v0.2.
  • FR-ENG-2: post-training transforms as blocks: quantization, pruning, format conversion (e.g. torch → onnx) — delegated to the relevant tool.

docs.title: 3.6 Model evaluation
docs.text:
• FR-EVL-1: standard metrics (accuracy, precision/recall/F1, ROC-AUC, RMSE, MAE, R²) — v0.1. In mallops-std, provided by std/evaluate.classification and std/evaluate.regression (feature evaluate, not in default; see std/evaluate).
  • FR-EVL-2: quality gates: a pipeline can skip downstream consumers or fail when a metric falls outside configured thresholds (min/max, v0.1); comparing against the current production model is deferred to v0.2 (with the model registry).
  • FR-EVL-3: custom metrics via plugins (in v0.1, external processes via std/external).
  • FR-EVL-4: explainability: model-agnostic feature importance (permutation importance over Predictor + evaluate metrics) as a block — v0.2.

docs.title: 3.7 Model packaging
docs.text:
• FR-PKG-1: package = self-contained format: dir artifact bundling a model, an optional fitted transform, optional metrics, and a deterministic package.json (schema_version: 1, flavor, composed io_schema, and embedded source IDs/manifests) with a Package::load helper — v0.1 (std/package, feature package, not in default; see std/package). Recording environment/runtime requirements is deferred to a later release.
  • FR-PKG-2: optional OCI image output for serving — v0.2.
  • FR-PKG-3: artifact signing (Sigstore/cosign or ed25519) — v0.3.

docs.title: 3.8 Model versioning
docs.text:
• FR-VER-1: model registry backed by the artifact store: name → versions → stages (staging, production, archived) — v0.2.
  • FR-VER-2: every version links to the run lineage that produced it (data hashes, code version, config).

docs.title: 3.9 Deploy
docs.text:
• FR-DEP-1: deploy targets as blocks: local process, Docker, Kubernetes manifest, SSH host, edge fleet — v0.2+.
  • FR-DEP-2: strategies: replace, canary, shadow — v0.3.
  • FR-DEP-4: remote execution of pipeline nodes (remote runners, Kubernetes jobs) — v0.3.
  • FR-DEP-3: rollback to a previous registry version in one command.

docs.title: 3.10 Model serving
docs.text:
• FR-SRV-1: HTTP/JSON inference server (mallops serve [PACKAGE_ID]) running as a native process outside the batch DAG, consuming a package artifact produced by mallops run (behind the serve-http Cargo feature of mallops-std; enabled in mallops-cli) — v0.1 (ADR-0007). Exposes GET /health (unauthenticated liveness/readiness probe reporting active package id and flavor) and POST /predict (single JSON object → object, array of objects → ordered array, [] → []; replays any bundled FittedTransform before calling Predictor), with optional bearer-token auth from MALLOPS_SECRET_<NAME>, body size limit (default 10 MiB), request timeout (default 30 s), concurrency cap (default 64), metadata-only request logs, --trust-unsafe-flavors enforcement, and zero-downtime SIGHUP hot-swap on Unix via runs/latest.json. See mallops serve.
  • FR-SRV-2: health/readiness probe (GET /health) in v0.1 (FR-SRV-1); gRPC endpoint and dynamic batching — v0.2.
  • FR-SRV-4: MQTT transport (serve.transport: mqtt): read requests from a topic, predict, publish to a response topic; at-least-once, acknowledged after the prediction is published — v0.3 (ADR-0009).
  • FR-SRV-3: backend-agnostic: the server dispatches to a Predictor chosen by the package flavor (smartcore, external Python process in v0.1; ort, tract, candle, burn, llama.cpp…) via PredictorRegistry::get. In v0.1 the minimal Predictor contract lives in mallops-std (shared by evaluate and serve) and is promoted to mallops-core before 1.0 (ADR-0007). See the Predictor contract reference.
  • FR-SRV-5: batch inference inside the DAG: apply a package (fitted transform + Predictor) to a dataset and emit the predictions as an artifact — v0.1 (std/predict.batch, #57).

docs.title: 3.11 Monitoring and logging
docs.text:
• FR-MON-1: structured logs (tracing) for every run and every request — v0.1.
  • FR-MON-2: Prometheus metrics and OpenTelemetry traces — v0.3.
  • FR-MON-3: data/prediction drift detection (PSI, KS test) as blocks — v0.3.

docs.title: 3.12 Retrain
docs.text:
• FR-RET-1: triggers as blocks: schedule (cron), drift alert, new data, manual — v0.3.
  • FR-RET-2: a trigger starts a pipeline run; evaluation gates decide promotion.

docs.title: 3.13 Edge
docs.text:
• FR-EDG-1: mallops-edge agent: single static binary, cross-compiled for aarch64/armv7/x86_64, inference-only by default (profile-edge of mallops-std, which includes HTTP and MQTT serving) — v0.4 (ADR-0008).
  • FR-EDG-2: local serving with any Predictor backend, offline-capable.
  • FR-EDG-3: distributed monitoring: nodes buffer metrics/drift stats locally and push them when connected.
  • FR-EDG-4: federated learning: central aggregator (FedAvg, FedProx as plugin), nodes train locally, only model updates leave the device; optional secure aggregation and differential privacy as plugins.
  • FR-EDG-5: fleet deploy: pull-based model updates with signature verification.
  • FR-EDG-6: on-device online learning (online feature): a finite DAG (ingest new labelled samples, e.g. from MQTT → train from the current model via an optional base input → evaluate gate → package) produces a new immutable package; serving hot-swaps to it only if the gate passes, with rollback and bounded retention (ADR-0008).

docs.title: 3.14 Lineage
docs.text:
• FR-LIN-1: the runtime emits lineage events (RunStarted, BlockStarted, ArtifactProduced, BlockFinished, RunFinished) with RFC 3339 UTC millisecond timestamps (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.mmmZ, computed from SystemTime without an external date crate) — v0.1. RunStarted carries pipeline_hash (domain-separated BLAKE3 "mallops pipeline v1" over canonical JSON of the topologically ordered nodes: id, use, BlockSpec.version, config_hash, in, seed), git_commit (None in the core library; populated by mallops-cli), and host (os, arch, hostname from HOSTNAME/COMPUTERNAME or "unknown", mallops_version). Each started node emits BlockStarted (block string, block_version, config_hash, seed, inputs), one ArtifactProduced per output (including cache hits), and BlockFinished (status, duration_ms, cached: true on cache hits). Nodes that never start (Skipped or Cancelled before execution) emit only BlockFinished with duration_ms: 0. RunFinished reports Cancelled if the run was cancelled, else Succeeded if RunSummary::is_success(), else Failed.
  • FR-LIN-2: events go to pluggable LineageSinks; the core ships JsonSink (default in RuntimeConfig::new), writing runs/<run-id>/lineage.json = {"v":1,"run":"<run-id>","events":[...]} (events internally tagged with "event" in snake_case) via ArtifactStore::put_meta, rewritten on every event so the file stays valid JSON after a crash — v0.1. mallops_core::lineage::conformance::check_sink provides a shared conformance suite reusable by future sinks. SQLite, OpenLineage and MLflow sinks are optional — v0.2+.
  • FR-LIN-5: experiment tracking: list and compare runs, their configs and metrics (mallops runs list/compare) on top of lineage and the SQLite sink — v0.2.
  • FR-LIN-3: multiple sinks can be active at once via RuntimeConfig::lineage (YAML lineage: mapping lives in mallops-cli); an empty sink list (lineage: off) disables lineage entirely while caching still works (it relies on artifact hashes and cache/<key>.json, not on lineage). A sink returning Err logs a tracing::warn! and never fails the run.
  • FR-LIN-4: secrets are never written to any sink, log, workdir, or store (verified by lineage_anti_leak_*).

docs.title: 4. Non-functional requirements
docs.text: Id Requirement NFR-1 Performance Core overhead per block < 5 ms (median on MemoryStore, checked by the ignored test runtime_nfr1_block_overhead); independent branches run in parallel. NFR-2 Reproducibility Same config + same input hashes + same seed ⇒ same artifact hashes for deterministic blocks; unchanged nodes are not re-executed: their outputs are served from the content-hash cache (NodeSummary.cached), cache: false or --no-cache (RuntimeConfig::no_cache) bypass it. NFR-3 Portability Linux, macOS, Windows; x86_64 and aarch64. Edge targets armv7. NFR-4 Security Secrets only via redacted ${secret:NAME} references (never written to config.json, cache keys, config_hash, logs, workdir, store, or lineage; checked by lineage_anti_leak_*); mallops.yaml, native blocks, and external processes are trusted code — sandboxing applies only to WASM plugins; unsafe code-executing model flavors require explicit opt-in at serve time; signed artifacts from v0.3. NFR-5 Observability Every run emits structured tracing logs (per-node node span, warnings on cache or lineage sink errors) and, unless lineage: off (RuntimeConfig::lineage empty), a lineage record (runs/<run-id>/lineage.json by default, rewritten incrementally per event). NFR-6 Stability Semantic versioning; public API of mallops-core frozen at 1.0 (#[non_exhaustive] on extensible public types). MSRV documented and tested in CI. NFR-7 Footprint mallops-core compiles without any ML, cloud-SDK, object_store, database, or HTTP/gRPC dependency; dependencies are restricted to the explicit allowlist (tokio, serde, serde_json, blake3, tracing, thiserror, ulid, tempfile) plus feature-gated yaml (yaml_serde, default) and schema (schemars, optional) (ADR-0007). NFR-8 Data scale In v0.1 the tabular std blocks load a whole dataset in memory (Arrow); streaming / out-of-core processing in chunked Arrow batches comes in v0.2, and larger-than-memory data can always go through std/external (Polars, DuckDB, Spark).

docs.title: 4.1 Trust model
docs.text:
mallops enforces explicit trust boundaries (ADR-0007):

  • Pipeline definitions (mallops.yaml) are trusted code. Running mallops run is equivalent to executing a build script: native blocks run in-process, external blocks run arbitrary configured commands (command:), and mallops run spawns git rev-parse HEAD (best-effort, in the directory of mallops.yaml, stderr discarded; failure yields None) to record RunStarted.git_commit. By contrast, mallops validate and mallops graph never execute user code, spawn external processes (not even git), or create the artifact store directory. mallops store verify likewise never runs blocks or spawns external processes.
  • Plugin isolation boundaries. Only WASM component plugins (post-v0.1) execute inside a capability-restricted sandbox. Native Rust blocks have no isolation; external CLI and gRPC blocks run as host processes. In v0.1, external CLI blocks execute via argv (never through a shell), with an explicit allowlisted environment and an isolated workdir, but this is process hygiene rather than a security sandbox.
  • Model flavor deserialization. Formats such as pickle, joblib, sklearn-pickle, and torchscript execute arbitrary code when loaded. Predictor implementations declare executes_code(&self) -> bool, and PredictorRegistry::get (used by mallops serve) refuses to load code-executing flavors (Error::Config) unless --trust-unsafe-flavors is explicitly passed. Prefer non-executing formats (onnx, safetensors, skops) and, from v0.3, cryptographically signed packages. See the Predictor contract reference.
  • Secrets. ${secret:NAME} references are resolved on demand through a SecretProvider (MALLOPS_SECRET_<NAME> environment variable in v0.1) into an opaque Secret newtype whose Debug/Display output is redacted ("***") and which does not implement Serialize. Secrets never enter Context.config, config.json, cache keys, config_hash, logs, or lineage sinks.
  • Store integrity. ArtifactId (strict 64 lowercase hex chars) and RelPath (relative POSIX UTF-8 path with no .. or root prefixes) are strictly validated. ArtifactStore rejects symlinks and special files, stores payloads read-only on LocalStore, and materializes copies on fetch so blocks can never mutate stored artifacts in place.

docs.title: 5. Pipeline definition (mallops.yaml)
docs.text:
version: 1
name: churn-classifier

store:                   # artifact store (optional, this is the default)
  kind: local            # local | memory | s3 | gcs | azure | plugin:<name>
  path: ./.mallops

lineage:                 # optional; default is [{ sink: json }]
  - sink: json
  - sink: openlineage
    with: { url: "${env:OPENLINEAGE_URL}" }
  # lineage: off         # disable completely

blocks:
  raw:
    use: std/ingest.csv
    with:
      path: data/customers.csv

  features:
    use: std/preprocess.tabular
    in: { data: raw.dataset }
    with:
      target: churned
      steps:
        - split: { test: 0.2, seed: 42 }     # optional `validation: 0.1` adds `features.validation`
        - impute: { strategy: median }
        - scale: { method: standard }

  model:
    use: std/external                  # any language, any library
    in: { train: features.train }
    with:
      command: ["python", "./train.py"]
      inputs: { train: features }
      outputs: { model: model }
      flavor: sklearn-pickle
      params: { n_estimators: 200 }

  eval:
    use: std/evaluate.classification
    in: { model: model.model, test: features.test }
    with:
      gate: { metric: f1, min: 0.80 }

  package:
    use: std/package
    in: { model: model.model, preprocess: features.transform, metrics: eval.metrics }

serve:                   # optional serving config read by `mallops serve` (not a DAG node)
  package: package.package
  host: 127.0.0.1
  port: 8080

Rules: - blocks: defines the finite batch DAG executed by mallops run. Long-running serving lives in the optional top-level serve: section (read by mallops serve, never started by mallops run). - use references a block by namespace/name, where name is stage[.variant] (e.g. std/ingest.csv, std/package). Each segment starts with [a-z0-9] and contains only [a-z0-9_-]; anything else fails as a malformed block reference (std/… built-in in v0.1; plugin/…, wasm:path.wasm, and grpc:host:port are reserved for post-v0.1 plugin runtimes and fail with a clear error in v0.1). - in wires named inputs to <block>.<output> (split at the first .); this defines the DAG. Cycles and self-loops are rejected. - with is block-specific config, validated by Block::validate_config (using serde in v0.1; optional JSON Schema validation behind the schema-validate feature). Each block also supports cache: false to bypass caching for that node and an optional seed: (u64) for deterministic blocks; the seed is part of the cache key, so changing it re-executes the node. The run-level --no-cache (RuntimeConfig::no_cache) bypasses the cache for every node. - Validation (PipelineConfig::validate, behind mallops validate) runs in one pass, never calls Block::run, and reports every problem at once as Error::Validation(Vec<ValidationError>), each with a dotted path: blocks.<id>.use (unknown block, or a Stage::Serve block, which is not a DAG node), blocks.<id>.in.<port> (malformed reference, unknown upstream node or output port, undeclared input port, kind/format/flavor mismatch, required input not connected), blocks.<id>.with[.<sub>] (errors of Block::validate_config and Block::resolve_ports, prefixed with blocks.<id>.with), blocks.<id> (one error per cycle, on its first node by id, listing the nodes) and serve.package (not <node>.<output>, unknown node or output, or kind other than package). A node whose block is unknown, is a Stage::Serve block, or whose with: fails validate_config or resolve_ports is unresolved: checks that need its ports (declared input ports, required inputs, output ports, kind/format/flavor compatibility of the edges touching it, serve.package pointing at it) are skipped, so one root cause yields one error. When validate_config fails, resolve_ports is not called. Nodes of the validated pipeline are in topological order, ties broken by node id. - Execution (Runtime::run, behind mallops run) runs nodes of the validated pipeline as soon as all their upstream nodes have finished, at most --jobs (RuntimeConfig::max_jobs, 0 counts as 1) blocks at a time, and returns a RunSummary with one NodeSummary per node: status (Succeeded, Failed, Skipped, Cancelled), duration, committed output ids, cached (outputs served from the cache), and a skip/cancel reason or the error. Node outcomes never make run return Err; only runtime failures do (for example, the run workdir cannot be created). Rules: - A node whose block or output commit fails is Failed; all its descendants are Cancelled without running, with a reason naming the failed node. Independent branches finish. - BlockOutcome::Skipped marks the node Skipped (outputs it still returns are committed). A consumer is Skipped without running when any required input comes from a Skipped node or was not committed, even if its other inputs succeeded (fan-in). An optional input without a committed artifact is simply absent. If a node has both a failed/cancelled and a skipped parent, it is Cancelled. For std/evaluate.* quality gates (gate: { metric, min?, max?, on_fail: skip | fail }, default skip), a failed skip gate commits metrics, blocks consumers that wire eval.metrics as a required input, and also causes std/package to return Skipped whenever metrics is wired (even though its metrics port is optional), leaving runs/latest.json unchanged; on_fail: fail returns Error::Block without committing metrics and cancels descendants (see std/evaluate). - Cancellation is cooperative: once the run's CancelToken fires, no new node starts (Cancelled, reason run cancelled); a running block that returns Error::Cancelled is Cancelled (not Failed). Nothing is aborted forcibly. - Output drafts are validated before any store.put (errors at out.<port>): every draft names a declared output port and satisfies its kind/format/flavor; a Produced outcome provides every required output; File/Dir payloads canonicalize inside the node workdir to a regular file / a directory, and the canonical path is what the store receives. The runtime sets parents to the node's input ids (sorted, deduplicated). Payload content (nested symlinks, special files inside a Dir) is checked by the store during put; if that fails the node is Failed, and outputs of the same node committed before stay in the store as unreferenced artifacts (immutable, harmless, removed by a later GC). - Cache (NFR-2): after the node gets its job slot, the cache is bypassed when cache: false is set or no_cache is on (Block::cache_policy is then not called); otherwise Block::cache_policy is consulted (an error fails the node; extra_hash must not depend on secrets) and Uncacheable bypasses it too. Otherwise a hit (all recorded output artifacts still in the store) marks the node Succeeded with cached: true, its outputs taken from the entry, and the block is not run; a miss runs it. Only Succeeded nodes are cached (Skipped, Failed, Cancelled always re-run). Failing to write the entry, or a store error while reading it (treated as a miss), is a warning, the node stays Succeeded. A rerun re-executes every node that did not succeed, plus the descendants whose inputs changed. - Each run gets a temporary workdir under RuntimeConfig::workdir_root (which may be relative) with one subdirectory per node; ctx.workdir() is always absolute and canonical. The run workdir is removed when the run ends. - Values may reference environment variables ${env:NAME} (resolved into config and included in config_hash; NAME is [A-Za-z0-9_]+; interpolated only in string values of each block's with, of lineage sink with, and in store.path, never in keys, in, seed or elsewhere; replaced text is not re-scanned; no escape syntax; a missing variable is an error naming the file and the block, sink or store.path) and secrets ${secret:NAME} (same NAME charset, validated at load; kept literally in the config, never resolved at load time; resolved on demand via MALLOPS_SECRET_<NAME> in v0.1 into a redacted Secret, never written to config.json, cache keys, logs, or lineage). - Unknown keys are rejected (deny_unknown_fields); lineage accepts only off or a list of sinks; version must be 1; duplicate block ids (or in ports) are rejected. Syntax and schema errors are reported as <file>:<line>:<column>: <message>. - Store and lineage backend mapping in the v0.1 CLI (check_backends, enforced by validate, run, and store verify): - store.kind accepts local (LocalStore at <yaml-dir>/<store.path>, where <yaml-dir> is the parent directory of the mallops.yaml path, defaulting to . when empty) and memory (MemoryStore). Any other store.kind fails with an error. - lineage: off disables lineage (RuntimeConfig::lineage = vec![]); otherwise every configured sink must have sink: json (JsonSink on the configured store). Any other sink name fails with an error. - Built-in blocks in mallops-cli: core/noop (version 1.0.0, Stage::Custom, optional input in: blob, output out: blob with format: noop and empty payload; test affordances fail: "<message>" and skip: "<reason>" in with:) plus all feature-enabled standard blocks registered via mallops_std::register_std(&mut registry) (in v0.1 so far: std/evaluate.classification, std/evaluate.regression, std/external, std/ingest.csv, std/ingest.parquet, std/package, std/preprocess.tabular, std/train.smartcore, std/validate.tabular). - Latest run pointer (runs/latest.json): after mallops run, if and only if every node is Succeeded, the CLI writes runs/latest.json via ArtifactStore::put_meta (meta/runs/latest.json on LocalStore) as {"v":1,"pipeline":"<name>","run":"<run-id>","outputs":{"<node>":{"<port>":"<artifact-id>"}}} (deterministic key order via BTreeMap), so mallops serve can resolve serve.package without an explicit id. If any node is Skipped (with no failed/cancelled nodes), mallops run leaves any previous runs/latest.json unchanged, prints latest.json not updated: <S> skipped, and exits 0. A failed run leaves any previous runs/latest.json unchanged and exits 1 (error: run failed). - A JSON Schema for mallops.yaml can be generated via the optional schema feature (schemars) for editor completion.

docs.title: 5.1 CLI (mallops)
docs.text:
Global flags: --version (-V), -v / --verbose (stderr tracing logs at DEBUG instead of WARN), and -f / --file <PATH> (default mallops.yaml).

Exit codes: 0 on success, 1 on configuration, validation, runtime, or store verification error, 2 on CLI argument/usage error (clap).

Command Behavior mallops init [DIR] Writes a minimal runnable mallops.yaml (two core/noop nodes, hello → world) into DIR (default ., creating missing parent directories); fails if mallops.yaml already exists. mallops validate Parses and validates mallops.yaml (including serve: if present) and checks supported store/lineage backends without executing blocks or spawning processes. Prints ok: <name> (<N> blocks) on stdout, or every validation error (error: <path>: <message>) on stderr. mallops run [--jobs N] [--no-cache] Validates and executes the batch DAG (blocks: only; ignores serve:). Changes the working directory to the directory of mallops.yaml so relative paths in block configs (such as std/ingest.* path) resolve against the pipeline directory, matching store.path. --jobs N overrides RuntimeConfig::max_jobs (default: available parallelism; 0 counts as 1); --no-cache bypasses the cache. Populates git_commit via best-effort git rev-parse HEAD in the mallops.yaml directory. Prints one line per node in topological order (<node> <status>[ (cached)] <ms>ms[: <reason/error>]) followed by run <run-id>: <E> executed, <C> cached, <F> failed, <S> skipped, <X> cancelled (executed = non-cached Succeeded). Writes runs/latest.json only when every node is Succeeded (if any node is Skipped, prints latest.json not updated: <S> skipped and exits 0); exits 1 on failure. Ctrl-C (SIGINT) cancels the run cooperatively through the run's CancelToken: running nodes end Cancelled (std/external kills its child's process group), the summary is printed and the exit code is 1. mallops graph [--format mermaid\|dot] Prints the validated DAG in topological order as Mermaid (flowchart TD, default) or Graphviz DOT (digraph), with edges labeled by input port name, without executing blocks or spawning processes. mallops blocks list Prints registered blocks (ID, VERSION, STAGE, INPUTS, OUTPUTS; optional inputs suffixed with ?, empty port list shown as -), sorted by block id. mallops store verify <ID> Parses <ID> as an ArtifactId, checks backends, opens the configured store (for kind: local, fails with store not found: <path> without creating it if absent), and calls ArtifactStore::verify. Prints ok: <id> on stdout on success; exits 1 on invalid id, missing store/artifact, or corruption/tampering. mallops serve [PACKAGE_ID] [--host HOST] [--port PORT] [--trust-unsafe-flavors] [--max-body-bytes N] [--timeout SECS] [--max-concurrency N] [--auth-token-secret NAME] Serves a package artifact over HTTP/1.1 (GET /health, POST /predict) as a native process outside the batch DAG (requires a persistent store; logs at INFO by default). Precedence: CLI flags > serve: in mallops.yaml > defaults (127.0.0.1:8080, 10 MiB, 30 s, 64). Without PACKAGE_ID, resolves serve.package from runs/latest.json (matching pipeline; otherwise error: no successful run: run \mallops run` first). Printsserving on http://, shuts down gracefully onCtrl-C/SIGTERM, and hot-swaps viaruns/latest.jsonon UnixSIGHUP(ignored with a warning whenPACKAGE_IDis explicit). See [mallops serve`](reference/serve.md).

docs.title: 6. Artifact contract
docs.text:
<store>/artifacts/<blake3-hash>/
├── manifest.json
└── payload/…          # any files, opaque to the core

{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "kind": "model",
  "format": "pickle",
  "flavor": "sklearn-pickle",
  "io_schema": { "input": [{"name": "age", "type": "f64"}], "output": [{"name": "churned", "type": "f64"}] },
  "metadata": { "framework": "scikit-learn", "framework_version": "1.6.0" },
  "parents": ["<hash>", "<hash>"]
}

Per-run provenance (run, node) is not part of manifest.json; it is recorded in LineageEvent::ArtifactProduced so identical deterministic runs produce identical ArtifactIds (ADR-0007). Cryptographic signatures (FR-PKG-3, v0.3) are stored alongside artifacts rather than inside manifest.json.

Canonical ArtifactId encoding (v1): 1. Initialize a BLAKE3 keyed hasher with blake3::derive_key("mallops artifact v1"). 2. Serialize Manifest as canonical compact JSON (object keys sorted by UTF-8 byte order, numbers in serde_json format — not RFC 8785 — io_schema: null omitted as absent, and parents sorted lexicographically and deduplicated) and hash u64::to_le_bytes(len) || manifest_json_bytes. 3. Collect all payload files via validated RelPath (relative UTF-8 POSIX paths with / separators, no .., no symlinks) sorted bytewise; hash u64::to_le_bytes(file_count) followed by len(path) || path || len(content) || blake3(content) for each file (all lengths as u64 little-endian). 4. Encode the 32-byte digest as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

kind Typical format values Notes dataset parquet, arrow-ipc, csv, json, images, tfrecord, any Arrow/Parquet is the interchange default for std blocks only (ADR-0002): std/ingest.* emit format: parquet with a single uncompressed payload/data.parquet file (created_by: "mallops-std", deterministic per mallops-std version, source schema metadata stripped) features as dataset preprocessed feature splits: std/preprocess.tabular emits format: parquet (payload/data.parquet, uncompressed) with metadata["target"] and io_schema: {"features": [{"name", "type"}], "target": {"name", "type"}} transform json, bin, pickle, any fitted preprocessor (scaler, imputer, encoder…) reused by package and serve: std/preprocess.tabular emits format: json (payload/transform.json = {"v":1,"target":…,"input":[…],"steps":[…]}) with io_schema: {"input": [{"name", "type"}], "output": [{"name", "type"}]} model json, onnx, safetensors, torchscript, pickle, joblib, gguf, xgboost-json, savedmodel, any flavor selects the predictor: std/train.smartcore emits format: json (payload/model.json), flavor: smartcore-logistic or smartcore-linear, and io_schema: {"input": [{"name", "type"}], "output": [{"name", "type"}]} (same shape as transform; see std/train.smartcore) metrics json key → number map + optional plots package dir, oci self-contained format: dir bundle (payload/package.json, model/, optional transform/ and metrics/) carrying flavor and composed io_schema (std/package); oci in v0.2 blob any escape hatch

Model flavor code-execution safety:

Flavor / format Executes code on load? Serving default onnx, safetensors, smartcore-*, xgboost-json, gguf, skops No Allowed pickle, joblib, sklearn-pickle, torchscript Yes Refused unless --trust-unsafe-flavors

Inputs and outputs of blocks declare the accepted kind and optionally accepted formats / flavors; mallops validate checks compatibility before running (using Block::resolve_ports when ports depend on with: config); an output is wired into an input only if its kind is equal and every format/flavor it may produce is accepted (an empty accepted list means any; an unconstrained output, i.e. an empty list, does not satisfy a constrained input). Error paths are listed in §5.

docs.title: 7. Roadmap
docs.text: Version Scope v0.1 mallops-core (Block trait, canonical artifacts, immutable ArtifactStore + local/memory + auxiliary metadata, explicit BlockRegistry, lineage events + JSON sink, DAG runtime, YAML), CLI (init, validate, run, graph, blocks list, store verify, serve), mallops-std (Predictor contract, ingest csv/parquet, preprocess tabular, train smartcore, generic external block, data validation, evaluate classification/regression, package, batch inference, HTTP serving) v0.2 remote store backends, SQLite/OpenLineage/MLflow lineage sinks, data storage blocks, model registry & versioning, hyperparameter search, deploy local/docker, gRPC serving, OCI packaging, WASM and gRPC plugin runtimes, experiment tracking, explainability, streaming / out-of-core std blocks v0.3 monitoring (Prometheus/OTel), drift detection, retrain triggers, DL training (burn/candle), signing, canary/shadow deploy, MQTT ingest/publish blocks and MQTT serving transport, remote execution of nodes v0.4 mallops-edge (edge build profiles), on-device online learning, federated learning, fleet deploy, distributed monitoring v1.0 stable public API, plugin protocol v1 frozen

docs.title: Commits and PR titles
docs.text: PRs are squash-merged, so the PR title becomes the commit and must follow Conventional Commits: feat(core): add artifact store, fix(cli): …, docs: …, refactor: …, test: …, ci: …, build: …, chore: …. Breaking changes: feat!: … or a BREAKING CHANGE: footer.

docs.title: Developer Certificate of Origin (DCO)
docs.text:
Every commit must be signed off, certifying that you wrote it or otherwise have the right to submit it under the project license, as stated in the Developer Certificate of Origin. The sign-off is a trailer matching the commit author:

Signed-off-by: Jane Doe <jane@example.com>

Add it with git commit -s. To fix commits already in a PR:

git rebase --signoff origin/dev        # adds the trailer to every commit of the branch
git push --force-with-lease

The dco CI job blocks PRs with unsigned commits and rejects merge commits in feature PRs (rebase onto dev instead; verified dependabot[bot]/github-actions[bot] commits and verified GitHub merge commits in release/back-merge PRs are exempt). Squash merges keep all trailers in the final commit.

docs.title: Local checks
docs.text:
cargo fmt --all
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --all-features

CI also runs, and ci-ok requires:

  • Coverage: cargo llvm-cov --workspace --all-features --fail-under-lines 85 (install with cargo install cargo-llvm-cov).
  • SAST: CodeQL (security-and-quality) on Rust and on the workflows; any error or warning fails the PR. Alerts are in the Security tab.
  • SCA: cargo deny check on the whole dependency tree (advisories, licenses, sources), plus GitHub dependency review on the dependencies a PR adds or updates.
  • Workflow security: zizmor on .github/ (uvx zizmor .; config in .github/zizmor.yml).

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
The site is built with MkDocs Material from docs/ and published on GitHub Pages, versioned with mike: /dev/ follows the dev branch, /X.Y/ is published at each release, /latest/ points to the newest stable one.

pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
mkdocs serve          # live preview on http://127.0.0.1:8000
mkdocs build --strict # what CI runs on PRs

The Rust API reference is generated by rustdoc and hosted on docs.rs.

docs.title: Releasing (maintainers)
docs.text:
1. Actions → Start release → choose patch|minor|major. This opens release/X.Y.Z → main and publishes vX.Y.Z-beta.1.
  2. Test the beta; push fixes to the release branch (each push = new beta).
  3. Merge the PR with Create a merge commit. The tag, GitHub Release, binaries and crates.io publish happen automatically.
  4. Merge the auto-opened back-merge PR into dev (merge commit).

Required secrets: RELEASE_TOKEN (repository secret, fine-grained PAT or GitHub App token with contents + pull-requests write, so bot-created branches/PRs trigger CI) and CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN (in the release environment, for crates.io).

docs.title: Architecture changes
docs.text: Significant design changes need an ADR in docs/adr/ submitted with or before the implementation.

docs.title: Architecture Decision Records
docs.text:
Format: MADR light. One decision per file, numbered, never edited after acceptance — supersede with a new ADR instead.

# Title Status 0001 Modular Cargo workspace Accepted 0002 Arrow/Parquet as default (not mandatory) data interchange Accepted 0003 Plugins via WASM components and external processes Accepted 0004 Format-agnostic artifacts with flavors Accepted 0005 GitFlow branching and automated releases Accepted 0006 Artifact store and lineage: contracts in the core, implementations pluggable Accepted 0007 Core contracts revision before v0.1 implementation Accepted 0008 Edge build profiles and on-device online learning Accepted 0009 MQTT blocks and MQTT serving transport Accepted

docs.title: 0001 — Modular Cargo workspace
docs.text: • Status: Accepted · 2026-11-20

docs.title: Context
docs.text: mallops must be usable as a library, with plugins, or standalone. Users should pay (compile time, binary size, dependencies) only for the blocks they use.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: A Cargo workspace with a small number of crates: mallops-core (no ML deps), mallops-std (standard blocks, each behind a feature flag), mallops-cli, and later mallops-edge. Crates are created only when they have code.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• cargo add mallops-std --features train-linfa,serve-http gives exactly what is needed.
  • Fewer crates = simpler releases. If mallops-std grows too heavy, per-stage crates can be split out without breaking users (re-exports).

docs.title: 0002 — Arrow/Parquet as default (not mandatory) data interchange
docs.text: • Status: Accepted · 2026-11-20

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Standard blocks need a common tabular representation to interoperate. At the same time mallops must not lock users into one data format.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Standard tabular blocks exchange data as Parquet files (on disk) and Arrow RecordBatch (in memory). This is a convention of mallops-std, not of the core: a dataset artifact can have any format, and blocks declare which formats they accept.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Zero-copy interop with Polars, DataFusion, DuckDB, pandas/pyarrow in external blocks.
  • Non-tabular data (images, audio, text corpora) flows as plain files with a declared format.
  • Format conversion is an explicit block, never implicit.

docs.title: 0003 — Plugins via WASM components and external processes
docs.text: • Status: Accepted · 2026-11-20

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Users need to add blocks without recompiling mallops, often in languages other than Rust (Python dominates ML). Rust has no stable ABI, so dylib plugins break across compiler versions.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Three plugin kinds, all exposed to the runtime through the same Block trait: 1. Native: Rust crates registered at compile time (inventory). 2. WASM components (wasmtime, WIT interface) for portable, sandboxed blocks. 3. External processes via a file-based CLI contract (inputs.json/config.json → outputs.json) and, for long-lived workers, a gRPC protocol.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Any language works through the external contract; a thin Python SDK is planned.
  • No dylib loading, no ABI issues.
  • The WIT and protobuf definitions become public API and are versioned with the core.

docs.title: 0004 — Format-agnostic artifacts with flavors
docs.text: • Status: Accepted · 2026-11-20

docs.title: Context
docs.text: ML teams use many model formats (ONNX, safetensors, TorchScript, pickle/joblib, GGUF, XGBoost JSON, SavedModel, custom). Picking one (e.g. ONNX) would exclude models that cannot be converted and force lossy conversions.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: An artifact is opaque payload files plus a manifest.json with kind, format, flavor and free-form metadata. The core never reads payloads. Model consumers (serving, evaluation, edge) select an implementation of the Predictor trait by flavor. Backends (ort, tract, candle, burn, linfa, llama.cpp, external Python workers…) are all equal plugins.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Any model, any library, any language.
  • Validation is limited to declared metadata; a block that receives an unsupported flavor fails early at mallops validate.
  • Conversions (e.g. torch → onnx) are explicit model-engineering blocks.

docs.title: 0005 — GitFlow branching and automated releases
docs.text: • Status: Accepted · 2026-11-20

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The project needs a clear contribution flow, stable releases, and a way to ship pre-releases for testing.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• main: only released code; every commit is a tag vX.Y.Z.
  • dev: default branch, integration of feature/* and fix/* via PR.
  • release/X.Y.Z: cut from dev by the Start release workflow; every push publishes a GitHub pre-release vX.Y.Z-beta.N. It acts as the beta channel, so no extra long-lived beta branch.
  • hotfix/*: from main, merged back to main and dev.
  • Conventional Commits enforced on PR titles (squash merge); changelog generated by git-cliff.
  • Merge of a release/hotfix PR into main tags, creates the GitHub Release with binaries, publishes crates, and opens a back-merge PR into dev.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• One click to start a release, zero manual tagging.
  • Squash merges keep history linear and changelog accurate.

docs.title: 0006 — Artifact store and lineage: contracts in the core, implementations pluggable
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted · 2026-11-21
  • Refines: 0001

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The first draft put the artifact store (on top of object_store) and the lineage store inside mallops-core. That contradicts the "small core, optional everything else" principle and drags cloud dependencies into every build.

Two alternatives were considered: 1. Make them blocks. Rejected: blocks are nodes of the DAG, while store and lineage act on every edge. If storage were an optional node, the runtime could not hand data from A to B, and caching/resume would depend on the user remembering to add it. Lineage needs the whole graph, which only the runtime sees; a block would have to rebuild it. 2. Keep full implementations in the core. Rejected: forces object_store and a lineage backend on every user.

The draft also mixed two different things: the data storage lifecycle stage (persisting user data) and the internal artifact store.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• The core defines the contracts: ArtifactStore and LineageSink traits, plus the LineageEvent type emitted by the runtime.
  • The core ships only minimal, dependency-free implementations: LocalStore (filesystem, default), MemoryStore (ephemeral), JsonSink (one lineage.json per run).
  • Remote stores (S3, GCS, Azure via object_store) and other lineage sinks (SQLite, OpenLineage, MLflow) are mallops-std features or plugins.
  • Lineage supports zero or more sinks; lineage: off disables it. Sink failures are warnings, never run failures.
  • "Data storage" as a lifecycle stage is an ordinary optional block that writes user data to external systems; it is unrelated to the artifact store.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• mallops-core has no cloud or database dependency.
  • Caching, resume and data hand-off always work, because the store mechanism cannot be removed — only its backend swapped.
  • Caching relies on artifact hashes, not lineage, so disabling lineage loses audit history but not performance.
  • ArtifactStore, LineageSink and LineageEvent become public API and must stay stable from 1.0.

docs.title: 0007 — Core contracts revision before v0.1 implementation
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted · 2026-11-21
  • Partially supersedes: 0003 (compile-time inventory registration; plugin isolation table), 0004 (Predictor placement in v0.1; manifest fields)
  • Refines: 0001, 0006

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
A pre-implementation design review of SPEC.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, and the existing ADRs uncovered eight structural defects in mallops-core contracts that would cause cascading breaking changes as soon as v0.1 development starts:

  1. Including produced_by.run inside the hashed Manifest breaks content addressing, deduplication, and caching; the hash framing itself was unspecified.
  2. NFR-7 restricted mallops-core to four crates while core features require additional infrastructure crates, serde_yaml is archived upstream, and schemars::Schema leaked into public signatures.
  3. ArtifactStore lacked real immutability on LocalStore, validated ID/path types, and an API for auxiliary metadata (cache index, lineage.json, model registry).
  4. Core trait and struct signatures (Block, BlockSpec, Context, Manifest, LineageEvent, Error) were missing versioning, skip outcomes, cancellation, secret isolation, runtime-managed output commits, #[non_exhaustive], ArtifactKind::Transform, and an unambiguous I/O schema field name.
  5. serve was modeled both as a batch DAG node and as a standalone CLI command.
  6. Predictor was placed in mallops-core before being validated against real backends and out of dependency order with evaluate.
  7. No explicit trust model existed for executable YAML pipelines, code-executing model flavors, or actual plugin isolation boundaries.
  8. Compile-time inventory registration is fragile under LTO/cross-compilation, breaks test isolation, and adds unnecessary complexity for v0.1.

docs.title: D1 — Canonical ArtifactId encoding without produced_by
docs.text:
Decision: - Remove produced_by (and all run-specific or timestamp fields) from the content-addressed Manifest. Per-run provenance (run, node, artifact) is recorded exclusively in LineageEvent::ArtifactProduced. - Define a canonical, cross-platform encoding for ArtifactId using BLAKE3 with domain separation (blake3::derive_key("mallops artifact v1")): 1. Serialize the canonical Manifest (schema_version, kind, format, flavor, io_schema, parents, metadata) as canonical JSON with sorted object keys (BTreeMap / RFC 8785) and parents sorted lexicographically by ArtifactId; feed u64::to_le_bytes(manifest_bytes.len()) || manifest_bytes. 2. Feed u64::to_le_bytes(file_count) followed by each payload file sorted bytewise by its validated POSIX UTF-8 relative path (RelPath, / separators): len(path) || path || len(content) || blake3(content) (all lengths as u64 little-endian). - Represent ArtifactId as a 32-byte BLAKE3 digest formatted as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

Rationale: Because produced_by.run changes on every execution, hashing it made two identical deterministic runs produce different ArtifactIds, breaking NFR-2, FR-STO-4 (content deduplication), and downstream caching. Domain separation, length-prefixed framing, canonical JSON key ordering, and POSIX path normalization prevent hash-boundary collisions and guarantee identical digests across Linux, macOS, and Windows.

docs.title: D2 — Explicit mallops-core dependency allowlist, YAML parser, and schema isolation
docs.text:
Decision: - Amend NFR-7 to distinguish forbidden dependency categories (no ML/tensor/dataframe libraries, no cloud SDKs, no object_store, no database drivers, no HTTP/gRPC servers) from an explicit core allowlist: - Default core dependencies: tokio, serde, serde_json, blake3, tracing, thiserror, ulid, tempfile. - Feature-gated dependencies: - yaml (enabled by default): yaml_serde (0.10). - schema (disabled by default): schemars for generating JSON Schema documents for editor completion. - schema-validate (disabled by default): optional JSON Schema validation engine when requested, rather than compiled into default builds. - Remove schemars::Schema from BlockSpec's public API; use Option<serde_json::Value> instead. In v0.1, with: configuration is validated by Block::validate_config(&self, config: &serde_json::Value) (typically via serde::Deserialize). - Avoid adding async-trait to mallops-core (use Pin<Box<dyn Future + Send + '_>> or a dual native/dyn trait pattern).

Rationale — YAML parser selection: - serde_yaml is archived and unmaintained upstream and depends on archived unsafe-libyaml (RUSTSEC-2024-0449), failing cargo deny. - serde_yml is archived and affected by an unsoundness advisory (RUSTSEC-2025-0068). - serde-saphyr (MIT OR Apache-2.0, pure Rust with #![forbid(unsafe_code)], configurable resource budgets against alias bombs) is a strong future candidate, but requires MSRV Rust 1.89, which exceeds the workspace MSRV of Rust 1.85. Because the YAML parser is not exposed in mallops-core's public API, migrating to serde-saphyr after an MSRV bump will be non-breaking. - serde_norway is a single-maintainer fork, whereas yaml_serde is stewarded by The YAML Organization (yaml/yaml-serde). - yaml_serde (0.10) is actively maintained by The YAML Organization, dual-licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0 (permitted by deny.toml), supports MSRV 1.82 (compatible with 1.85), replaces unsafe-libyaml with libyaml-rs, has no active RustSec advisories, enforces recursion depth limits, and reports line/column locations on syntax errors. Parser tests must still explicitly cover YAML alias bombs and deeply nested inputs.

Keeping schemars out of public types protects mallops-core semver stability at 1.0 and keeps BlockSpec compatible with dynamic WASM/gRPC plugins.

docs.title: D3 — Immutable ArtifactStore, validated ArtifactId/RelPath, and auxiliary metadata API
docs.text:
Decision: - Introduce validated newtypes in mallops-core: - ArtifactId: 32-byte digest with strict FromStr (exactly 64 lowercase hex chars) and no unchecked string constructor. - RelPath: validated relative path (non-empty UTF-8, normalized / separators, rejecting .., leading /, Windows drive letters/backslashes, NUL bytes, and empty segments). - Harden ArtifactStore semantics: - put(&self, manifest: Manifest, payload: PayloadSource<'_>) -> Result<ArtifactId> accepts a structured PayloadSource (File, Dir, Bytes, or multi-file map), writes atomically (temp directory on the same filesystem + idempotent rename), rejects symlinks and special files, and verifies canonical paths stay inside the root. LocalStore::put marks stored files read-only (0444) and directories (0555) where supported by the OS. - get(&self, id: &ArtifactId) -> Result<Option<Artifact>> avoids exists + get TOCTOU races. - fetch(&self, id: &ArtifactId, dest: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf> has uniform semantics across all backends: it always materializes the payload into dest (read-only copy/materialization on LocalStore, download + integrity check on remote stores) and never returns a writable path inside the store itself. - verify(&self, id: &ArtifactId) -> Result<()> recomputes the canonical ArtifactId to detect corruption or tampering. - Add an auxiliary key-value metadata API on the store (or companion MetaStore contract implemented by every backend): put_meta, get_meta, list_meta, and delete_meta keyed by RelPath. Caching (cache/<key>.json), JsonSink (runs/<run-id>/lineage.json), and the v0.2 model registry (registry/<model>/<version>.json) all persist through this API.

Rationale: Making fetch a no-op on LocalStore allowed external blocks to mutate stored payloads in place, silently corrupting content addressing and cache integrity. Validated ArtifactId/RelPath types and symlink rejection close path-traversal and file-exfiltration vectors across LocalStore and external outputs.json. An explicit auxiliary metadata API ensures caching and JsonSink work identically across LocalStore, MemoryStore, and future remote stores without hardcoded filesystem paths.

docs.title: D4 — Core signatures (BlockSpec, Block, Context, Error, #[non_exhaustive], Transform, io_schema)
docs.text:
Decision: - BlockSpec: add version: Cow<'static, str>, use Cow<'static, str> for id and port/format/flavor strings, replace config_schema with Option<serde_json::Value>, return &BlockSpec from Block::spec(&self), and add optional hooks Block::validate_config(&self, config: &serde_json::Value) and Block::resolve_ports(&self, config: &serde_json::Value) for config-driven blocks (such as std/train.external). - BlockOutcome & cache_policy: Block::run returns Result<BlockOutcome> where BlockOutcome has Produced(OutputDrafts) and Skipped { reason: String, outputs: OutputDrafts }. Any downstream node with a required input from a skipped node is automatically skipped with Status::Skipped in lineage. Add Block::cache_policy(&self, ctx: &Context) -> Result<CachePolicy> (Deterministic { extra_hash: Option<Digest> } | Uncacheable) so source/external blocks invalidate when local files or scripts change. - Runtime-owned output commits: blocks produce output drafts (OutputDraft { manifest_draft, payload }); the runtime commits them to ArtifactStore, injects Manifest.parents from the node's actual input ArtifactIds, validates outputs against resolved ports, and emits LineageEvent::ArtifactProduced. Blocks never call store.put() directly for outputs. - Context: - Remove pub span: tracing::Span (the runtime wraps block.run(...).instrument(node_span).await). - Add cancel: CancelToken (cooperative cancellation built on tokio::sync::watch::Receiver<bool>). - Separate ${env:NAME} (interpolated into config and hashed into config_hash) from ${secret:NAME} (resolved on demand via ctx.secret("NAME") -> Result<Secret>, backed in v0.1 by a SecretProvider reading MALLOPS_SECRET_<NAME>).
