Secret is an opaque newtype with redacted Debug/Display ("***"), does not implement Serialize, and is excluded from config.json, cache keys, config_hash, logs, and lineage. - Provide ctx.config_as::<T>() for typed config deserialization. - mallops_core::Error: define a structured thiserror error enum (Config, Validation, Store, Runtime, Cancelled, Secret, InvalidArtifactId, InvalidPath, Block { id, source }). - #[non_exhaustive]: mark extensible public enums and structs (BlockSpec, BlockOutcome, Context, Artifact, Manifest, ArtifactKind, Stage, LineageEvent, Status, Error, CachePolicy, PayloadSource) as #[non_exhaustive] with dedicated constructors/builders. - ArtifactKind::Transform: add transform to ArtifactKind for fitted preprocessors consumed by package and serve. - Manifest.io_schema: rename Manifest.signature to Manifest.io_schema, reserving signature for cryptographic artifact signatures (FR-PKG-3, v0.3). - LineageEvent: add timestamp, block_version, seed: Option<u64>, Status::Skipped, and use Digest consistently instead of an undefined Hash type.

Rationale: These additions eliminate every known breaking gap between core issues (#1–#9) and downstream std/serving issues (#11–#17), prevent secret leakage and async tracing corruption, guarantee consistent parents and lineage events, and make the core API evolvable toward 1.0 under cargo-semver-checks.

docs.title: D5 — serve outside the batch DAG
docs.text:
Decision: - Remove serve from the batch DAG (blocks: in mallops.yaml). mallops run executes the finite batch DAG and produces a package artifact (gated by eval). - mallops serve [package-id] is a separate long-running command that consumes a package artifact. An optional top-level serve: section in mallops.yaml configures defaults (target package output, bind address, port) for mallops serve without participating in mallops run.

Rationale: A long-running HTTP server cannot be a normal batch DAG node: either it blocks mallops run indefinitely (preventing RunFinished and mallops run && mallops serve) or requires ad-hoc skipping rules. Separating batch production (run → package) from online inference (serve) gives both commands clear, composable semantics.

docs.title: D6 — Minimal Predictor contract in mallops-std for v0.1
docs.text:
Decision: - Partially supersede ADR-0004 for v0.1: keep Predictor (and LoadedPredictor) out of mallops-core and define a minimal contract in mallops-std shared by both evaluate and serve (implemented prior to evaluate). - Include flavors(&self) -> &[&str], executes_code(&self) -> bool, structured payloads (Json and Bytes), and batch inference (predict_batch). - Promote Predictor into mallops-core only before v1.0, once validated across multiple backends (linfa, external Python worker, ort/gRPC).

Rationale: Freezing Predictor in mallops-core before implementing a single backend or gRPC/binary inference risks an early breaking change (for example, locking into JSON-only payloads). Defining it first in mallops-std before evaluate fixes the dependency inversion between evaluate and serve while keeping mallops-core minimal.

docs.title: D7 — Explicit Trust model and corrected NFR-4
docs.text:
Decision: - Add a Trust model section to SPEC.md defining explicit trust boundaries: 1. mallops.yaml is trusted executable configuration: mallops run executes native blocks and external commands with host privileges, whereas mallops validate and mallops graph never execute user code or external processes. 2. Only WASM component plugins (post-v0.1) provide sandboxing. Native Rust blocks and external CLI/gRPC processes are trusted code (external CLI blocks run via argv without a shell, with an allowlisted environment and isolated workdir, but are not a security sandbox). 3. Model flavors that execute code on deserialization (pickle, joblib, sklearn-pickle, torchscript) are flagged (executes_code = true). mallops serve refuses to load them unless explicitly opted in via --trust-unsafe-flavors. Non-executing formats (onnx, safetensors, skops) and signed packages (v0.3) are recommended. 4. Secrets never enter Context.config, config.json, cache keys, logs, or lineage; ArtifactStore enforces validated paths, symlink rejection, and read-only storage. - Update NFR-4 in SPEC.md to reflect these exact guarantees instead of claiming sandboxing for all plugins.

Rationale: Documenting trust boundaries up front prevents false security assumptions (especially around pickle serving and external commands) and ensures v0.1 CLI and store implementations enforce safe defaults from day one.

docs.title: D8 — Explicit BlockRegistry in v0.1 (no inventory)
docs.text:
Decision: - Partially supersede ADR-0003 for v0.1: mallops-core provides an explicit, instance-local BlockRegistry populated via registry.register(...). - mallops-std exposes pub fn register_std(registry: &mut BlockRegistry) registering all feature-enabled standard blocks; mallops-cli and library callers invoke it explicitly. - Compile-time auto-registration (such as inventory behind an optional feature) is deferred until post-v0.1 if multi-crate ergonomics justify its trade-offs.

Rationale: inventory relies on linker ctor sections that can be silently stripped under LTO or unused-symbol elimination, behave inconsistently across static/cross-compilation/WASM targets, introduce global state that hurts test isolation, and add an unsafe-containing dependency to mallops-core. Explicit registration is deterministic, zero-magic, and trivial for v0.1's standard library.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• mallops-core contracts are internally consistent across artifacts, store, blocks, config, caching, lineage, and serving before issue #1 begins.
  • mallops-core remains free of ML, cloud, database, and HTTP/gRPC dependencies while gaining a realistic, auditable infrastructure allowlist.
  • ArtifactId digests are deterministic, cross-platform, and deduplicated across runs.
  • LocalStore and external blocks have enforceable immutability and path-traversal protections.
  • BlockRegistry is isolated and deterministic in unit and integration tests.
  • Accepted ADRs 0001–0006 remain untouched per MADR policy; this ADR records all supersessions and refinements.

docs.title: 0008 — Edge build profiles and on-device online learning
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted · 2026-11-22
  • Refines: 0001, 0007 (D5, D6)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The target scenario is "train on a server, deploy to edge devices, keep learning on the device". ADR-0007 D5 already separates the two sides: mallops run executes the batch DAG and produces a package, and mallops serve consumes it. ADR-0001 makes every standard block a feature of mallops-std.

Three things are still undefined: 1. ARCHITECTURE.md says mallops-edge depends on "std (subset)" but never names the subset. Without a defined profile, an edge build can pull in training dependencies (polars, external trainer) by accident. 2. Training on the device is mentioned only for federated learning (FR-EDG-4). On-device online learning, where the model adapts to local data and no aggregator is involved, is not covered. 3. It is not specified how a model that changes on the device stays consistent with D5 (serving is not a DAG node) and with the immutable store.

docs.title: D1 — Named feature profiles in mallops-std
docs.text:
mallops-std exposes profile features that only combine existing per-block features:

Profile Contents Excludes profile-server ingest, preprocess, train-*, evaluate, package, serve-http — profile-edge serve-http, pure-Rust predictors (predict-linfa, predict-tract), transform runtime, local metrics buffer every train-*, train-external, predict-external

Profiles are shortcuts. A user can always enable individual features instead. predict-tract adds the tract dependency, which needs approval when it is implemented.

docs.title: D2 — mallops-edge is inference-only by default
docs.text:
• Default features: profile-edge. A default build contains no training code, so there is nothing to disable at runtime.
  • online: on-device online learning (D3). It enables only the train-* features of backends that support incremental updates (D4).
  • fl: federated client (local training, sends only weight deltas to the aggregator, FR-EDG-4).

docs.title: D3 — On-device online learning is a finite DAG, never a mutation inside serving
docs.text:
On a device, online learning (and each federated round) runs as an ordinary finite DAG in the device LocalStore. mallops-edge starts it on a trigger (schedule, number of new labelled samples, aggregator round):

ingest(new labelled samples, e.g. std/ingest.mqtt, ADR-0009) → preprocess(reuse transform) → train(base = model of the current package) → evaluate(gate on local holdout) → package
  • base input port. A train block that supports incremental updates (partial_fit, warm start) declares an optional input port named base (kind model). The name is a convention of mallops-std, opt-in per block: a block that cannot update incrementally does not declare it, so wiring base into it fails at validation (blocks.<id>.in.base, undeclared input port). No core change is needed.
  • Every update produces a new immutable package with normal lineage (its parents include the previous package's model). The model being served is never changed in place.
  • Gate and hot-swap. The local serving loop switches to the new package only if the evaluate gate passes. Otherwise the run ends with the gate failure and the current package stays active.
  • Rollback goes back to the last package that passed the gate, or to the base package pulled from the registry.
  • Retention. The device keeps the active package, the previous accepted one and the base package; older accepted packages are garbage-collected (ties to FR-STO-5).
  • Reporting. By default the device reports only the metrics of each update (FR-EDG-3 buffer). Pushing accepted packages back to the registry is opt-in, because it sends a model derived from local data off the device.
  • Under fl, the aggregator round replaces the package step: the device sends the delta and, once aggregation completes, pulls the new global package.

docs.title: D4 — Portable flavors for edge
docs.text: Packages meant for edge should use non-code-executing, pure-Rust-servable flavors (onnx via tract, linfa-*). Online learning on the device additionally needs a flavor whose train block declares base (in practice linfa-* models with incremental fitting; onnx is inference-only). predict-external (Python worker) is not part of profile-edge. ADR-0007 D7 still applies: code-executing flavors are refused unless explicitly opted in.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• An edge binary is inference-only by construction. CI adds a check that cargo tree -p mallops-edge -e normal with default features contains no train-* dependency, plus an aarch64/armv7 cross-check of the default build.
  • D5 still holds: serving never becomes a DAG node, and on-device learning reuses the runtime, store, lineage, validation and gates unchanged.
  • Device storage is bounded by the retention rule of D3.
  • Incremental training becomes an optional capability of train blocks (base input). Not every backend supports it, and the validator reports misuse.
  • SPEC.md (§3.13, roadmap) and ARCHITECTURE.md (§2, §8) are updated together with this ADR.

docs.title: 0009 — MQTT blocks and MQTT serving transport
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted · 2026-11-22
  • Refines: 0006, 0007 (D5, D7), 0008

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Edge and IoT deployments usually move data over an MQTT broker. The reference scenario: on an edge device a sensor publishes readings to a topic, mallops reads them, the model predicts, and the predictions are published to another topic. The same data, once labelled, feeds on-device online learning (ADR-0008). FR-ING-3 already lists MQTT as an ingest source. mallops needs to: 1. read messages from MQTT topics into a pipeline (training data, online learning); 2. write pipeline results (datasets, predictions, metrics) to MQTT topics; 3. serve inference over MQTT: request topic in, prediction topic out.

MQTT is an unbounded stream, while the mallops run DAG is finite and batch, and serving is not a DAG node (ADR-0007 D5). So MQTT appears in two places: bounded blocks inside the DAG, and a serving transport outside it.

docs.title: D1 — std/ingest.mqtt: bounded read into a dataset
docs.text:
• Subscribes to one or more topic filters and stops at the first bound reached: max_messages, max_duration, or idle_timeout. At least one bound is required (validate_config), otherwise the run would never finish.
  • Produces a dataset artifact (format: jsonl by default, or parquet when the payload schema is declared) and records topic, timestamp and QoS per message.
  • cache_policy returns Uncacheable: the same config reads different messages each time. Once ingested, the data is content-addressed like any other dataset, so downstream nodes cache normally and the run is reproducible from the stored dataset.
  • Delivery. QoS 1 with a persistent session (clean_session: false, fixed client_id), so messages published while no run is active are kept by the broker. The block acknowledges messages only after its output draft is complete, just before returning. This gives at-least-once up to the block's return: a crash or a cancelled run before that point redelivers the messages on the next run. Blocks cannot observe the runtime commit (ADR-0007), so if the commit itself fails after the block returned, that batch is lost. This window is accepted and documented; closing it needs a post-commit hook in the core and is left to a later ADR if real deployments need it. Exactly-once is not offered: consumers dedupe by message id or payload.

docs.title: D2 — std/storage.mqtt: publish an artifact to a topic
docs.text:
• An ordinary optional data-output block with Stage::DataStorage (the same category as FR-STO-1, not the artifact store; see ADR-0006). No new stage is introduced.
  • Publishes one message per row of a dataset/features artifact (or one per artifact for metrics) to a topic template (e.g. devices/{device_id}/predictions) with the configured QoS and retain; with QoS 1 it waits for every PUBACK before returning.
  • Publishing is an external side effect: cache_policy returns Uncacheable, so a cache hit never silently skips publishing.
  • Output: a small metrics artifact (messages published, failures), so the node fits the DAG and the outcome is recorded in lineage.

docs.title: D3 — MQTT as a serving transport, not a block
docs.text:
• mallops serve and the mallops-edge serving loop get an mqtt transport next to http. It subscribes to a request topic, runs each message through the package's LoadedPredictor, and publishes the prediction to a response topic. This covers the sensor → predict → publish scenario without any DAG.
  • Configured in the top-level serve: section and never started by mallops run:
serve:
  package: package.bundle
  transport: mqtt              # default: http
  mqtt:
    url: mqtts://broker.local:8883
    client_id: edge-01
    request_topic: sensors/+/readings
    response_topic: predictions/{topic.1}   # or the MQTT v5 response_topic of the request
    qos: 1
    password: ${secret:MQTT_PASSWORD}
  • Delivery. Requests are read with QoS 1 and acknowledged only after the prediction has been published (and acknowledged by the broker at QoS 1), so every reading gets at least one prediction. Each response carries the request's MQTT v5 correlation_data when present, or its topic and message id, so consumers can dedupe.
  • A reading that fails validation or prediction produces an error message on {response_topic}/error (configurable) instead of being dropped silently.
  • Under mallops-edge, the same connection can optionally push the buffered metrics (FR-EDG-3) to a topic. gRPC stays the default for the fleet control plane and FL.

docs.title: D4 — Shared connection config, secrets and security
docs.text:
• A single mqtt connection schema is used by D1, D2 and D3: url (mqtt:// / mqtts://), client_id, keep_alive, tls (CA, client cert), username, password.
  • password and the client key accept only ${secret:NAME} and are resolved through ctx.secret() (or the same secret provider in serve). A literal value is rejected. Secrets never appear in config.json, cache keys or lineage.
  • mqtts:// is recommended. A plaintext mqtt:// connection to a non-loopback host emits a warning.
  • Incoming payloads are untrusted input: size limit (max_payload_bytes) and schema validation (the package io_schema in D3) before the data reaches the predictor or the dataset.

docs.title: D5 — Implementation and dependencies
docs.text:
• Lives in mallops-std behind features ingest-mqtt, storage-mqtt, serve-mqtt. serve-mqtt is part of profile-edge (ADR-0008), since sensor-driven inference is the main edge scenario.
  • Proposed client: rumqttc (pure Rust, tokio, MQTT 3.1.1 + 5, rustls). It must be approved as a new dependency and pass cargo deny when implemented. mallops-core gains no dependency; only ServeConfig grows the transport and mqtt fields.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• MQTT data enters and leaves the pipeline as ordinary artifacts, so lineage, hashing and caching downstream are unchanged.
  • Re-running a pipeline with ingest.mqtt is not reproducible from config alone; reproducibility comes from the stored dataset artifact, as for any live source.
  • Duplicates are possible on every MQTT path (at-least-once), and D1 has a documented loss window on commit failure; both are stated in the user docs.
  • Integration tests need a broker: an in-process broker (e.g. rumqttd as a dev-dependency) in CI.
  • SPEC.md (FR-ING-3, FR-STO-1, §3.10, §3.13, roadmap) and ARCHITECTURE.md (§7, §8) are updated together with this ADR.
  • A future streaming runtime (continuous DAG) could replace the bounded ingest of D1; this ADR deliberately does not introduce one.

docs.title: std/evaluate (std/evaluate.classification and std/evaluate.regression)
docs.text:
Model evaluation and quality-gate blocks for classification and regression. Behind the optional evaluate Cargo feature of mallops-std (evaluate = ["predictor", "_ingest", "dep:arrow-select"], not in default, no new crate dependency; enabled in mallops-cli together with predict-smartcore and predict-external). See SPEC FR-EVL-1 / FR-EVL-2.

blocks:
  eval:
    use: std/evaluate.classification
    in: { model: model.model, test: features.test }
    with:
      target: churned
      positive: true
      gate:
        metric: f1
        min: 0.80
        on_fail: skip

For regression:

blocks:
  eval:
    use: std/evaluate.regression
    in: { model: model.model, test: features.test }
    with:
      gate:
        metric: rmse
        max: 0.25
        on_fail: fail

docs.title: Configuration (with:)
docs.text:
Unknown fields are rejected (deny_unknown_fields). validate_config uses the same parser as run, so mallops validate catches configuration errors before execution.

Field Type Default Meaning target non-empty string none Target column name. Falls back to metadata["target"] of the test input artifact if omitted; if absent in both, or if both are set and differ, the run fails. positive JSON scalar (int64, bool, or string) none Classification only. Explicit positive class label for binary classification. Rejected on std/evaluate.regression and on multiclass (> 2 classes) classification. gate object none Optional quality gate: { metric, min?, max?, on_fail? }.

docs.title: gate fields
docs.text:
Key Type Default Constraints metric string required Must be a metric of the block's task (accuracy, precision, recall, f1, roc_auc for classification; rmse, mae, r2 for regression). min f64 none Finite inclusive lower bound (value >= min). max f64 none Finite inclusive upper bound (value <= max). on_fail skip | fail skip Action when the gate check fails.

Validation rules (validate_config):

  • A gate metric not belonging to the block's task is rejected.
  • gate must specify at least one of min or max. Specifying both is allowed (closed interval [min, max], endpoints inclusive) as long as min <= max.
  • Non-finite min or max values (NaN, ±inf) are rejected.
  • Setting positive on std/evaluate.regression is rejected.
  • Strings containing ${secret: anywhere in the config are rejected (as in std/external).

docs.title: Ports
docs.text:
Both blocks have version: "0.1.0" and Stage::Evaluate:

  • Block IDs: std/evaluate.classification, std/evaluate.regression.
  • Inputs:
  • model (required): kind: model, any format, any flavor (dispatched at runtime through PredictorRegistry).
  • test (required): kind: features, format: parquet.
  • Output:
  • metrics: kind: metrics, format: json.

docs.title: Execution and input data rules
docs.text:
• Predictor resolution: model is fetched into model/ and test into test/ inside ctx.workdir(). The predictor is resolved via predictors.get(flavor, true): mallops run executes trusted pipeline definitions (SPEC §4.1), so code-executing flavors such as sklearn-pickle are allowed during evaluation. A missing flavor in the model manifest is an error. Without any predict-* feature enabled in mallops-std, the blocks still register but fail at runtime with "no predictor for flavor \`"`.
  • Target resolution: uses with.target when set, otherwise metadata["target"] (string) from the test input artifact manifest. Missing in both is an error; present in both with different values is an error.
  • Test dataset: the entire test Parquet file is loaded into memory. Empty datasets (0 rows) fail with Error::Runtime.
  • Feature columns sent to the predictor:
  • If model.manifest.io_schema.input is a JSON array of column names, exactly those columns are sent. Each entry is either a string or an object with a name (the { "name", "type" } form written by std/train.smartcore). A missing column, or an empty array, fails with Error::Runtime.
  • Otherwise, every column in the test Parquet schema except the target column is sent.
  • Supported Arrow feature column types are Int64, Float64, Boolean, and Utf8. Nulls are encoded as JSON null; non-finite Float64 values (NaN, ±inf) are also encoded as JSON null (leaving handling to the predictor). Any other Arrow type (including Date32) fails with Error::Runtime.
  • Prediction call: each row is encoded as PredictInput::Json ({ "<col>": <val>, ... }) and evaluated in a single LoadedPredictor::predict_batch call.
  • outputs.len() must equal the number of input rows, otherwise Error::Runtime.
  • Every output must be a PredictInput::Json object containing prediction (and optional probability), otherwise Error::Runtime.
  • Cancellation: ctx.cancel() is checked at run start, after fetching inputs, and after predict_batch.

docs.title: Metrics semantics
docs.text: Every computed metric must be finite; a non-finite metric (NaN, ±inf, e.g. from floating-point overflow) fails with Error::Runtime regardless of gate.on_fail.

docs.title: Classification (std/evaluate.classification)
docs.text:
• Target (y_true): Arrow Int64, Boolean, or Utf8. Float64 and null values are Error::Runtime.
  • Label typing and class set: labels are parsed into a typed enum (int64, bool, or string). Every predicted prediction value and with.positive (if configured) must have the same type as y_true, otherwise Error::Runtime. The class set is the sorted set of distinct values in y_true ∪ y_pred (plus {with.positive} when set).
  • Binary (<= 2 classes):
  • positive is with.positive when configured, otherwise the greater class (classes[1], matching smartcore and scikit-learn). If only one class is present and with.positive is omitted, the run fails with Error::Runtime (cannot infer the positive class).
  • accuracy, precision, recall, f1 are computed with respect to positive; a division by zero yields 0.0 (matching scikit-learn's zero_division=0).
  • roc_auc is computed by Mann-Whitney ranks (average ranks for ties) only when all of the following hold: the task is binary, every output carries a valid probability, and y_true contains both classes. Per the Predictor contract, probability is P(classes[1]) (the greater class); when positive is the smaller class (classes[0]), 1 - p is used. If probability is absent from all rows or y_true contains only one class, roc_auc is omitted. If probability is present in only some rows, or is non-numeric, non-finite, or outside [0.0, 1.0], the run fails with Error::Runtime.
  • Multiclass (> 2 classes):
  • Setting with.positive fails with Error::Runtime.
  • accuracy plus macro-averaged precision, recall, f1 (division by zero yields 0.0).
  • roc_auc is omitted.

docs.title: Regression (std/evaluate.regression)
docs.text:
• Target (y_true): Arrow Int64 or Float64 cast to f64 (nulls and non-finite values fail with Error::Runtime).
  • Predictions (y_pred): prediction must be a finite JSON number (nulls and non-finite values fail with Error::Runtime).
  • Metrics: rmse, mae, r2.
  • Constant y_true: when y_true has zero variance, r2 is 1.0 if all residuals are 0.0 and 0.0 otherwise (matching scikit-learn's force_finite=True).

docs.title: Output (metrics.json) and manifest
docs.text:
The output artifact payload is a single file, metrics.json, containing a flat JSON object mapping computed metric names to finite f64 values with keys sorted lexicographically:

{
  "accuracy": 0.92,
  "f1": 0.89,
  "precision": 0.91,
  "recall": 0.87,
  "roc_auc": 0.95
}

Output manifest fields:

  • kind: metrics
  • format: json
  • metadata:
  • task: "classification" or "regression"
  • target: target column name
  • rows: number of evaluated rows
  • positive: positive class label (present only for binary classification)
  • gate: present only when with.gate is configured ({ "metric", "min"?, "max"?, "on_fail", "passed" })
  • No timestamps, run IDs, or block-written parents (the runtime injects parents on commit).

docs.title: Quality gate semantics
docs.text:
When with.gate is configured:

  • If the gate's metric was not computed at runtime (for example roc_auc in multiclass classification or when the predictor does not emit probabilities), the block returns Error::Config regardless of on_fail.
  • The gate passes iff min.is_none_or(|m| v >= m) && max.is_none_or(|m| v <= m) (inclusive endpoints; non-finite metrics fail before the gate check).
  • Passed: returns BlockOutcome::Produced with metrics.
  • Failed with on_fail: skip (default):
  • Returns BlockOutcome::Skipped { reason, outputs } (e.g. "gate failed: f1 = 0.75 < min 0.8"). The metrics artifact is still committed to the store so the failed evaluation can be inspected.
  • Downstream blocking: the runtime skips downstream nodes that consume eval.metrics as a required input. In addition, std/package checks metadata.gate.passed on a wired metrics input even though its metrics port is optional, so a package that wires metrics: eval.metrics (as in SPEC §5) is Skipped when the gate failed; a package that omits metrics still runs.
  • runs/latest.json and serving: when any node is Skipped, mallops run exits 0 but leaves runs/latest.json unchanged, so mallops serve continues serving the previous accepted package.
  • Caching: Skipped nodes are never cached by the runtime, so a failed gate is re-evaluated on the next run.
  • Failed with on_fail: fail:
  • Returns Error::Block { id, source: reason }. The runtime marks the node Failed, cancels all descendants, does not commit metrics (outputs are only committed on Ok), leaves runs/latest.json unchanged, and mallops run exits 1.

docs.title: Cache
docs.text:
CachePolicy::Deterministic { extra_hash: None }.

  • Same inputs, config, node seed:, and block version hit the cache when the previous run Succeeded. Skipped and Failed runs are never cached.
  • Changing metric computation semantics requires bumping BlockSpec.version.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Situation Error Unknown field, invalid gate metric for task, neither min nor max set, min > max, non-finite min/max, positive on regression, ${secret: in config Error::Config (in mallops validate, aggregated into Error::Validation under blocks.<id>.with) Missing predictor for model flavor (including when no predict-* feature is enabled) Error::Config Gate metric not available at runtime (e.g. roc_auc omitted) Error::Config Missing flavor in model manifest, missing target, with.target differing from metadata["target"], or missing column Error::Runtime Unsupported Arrow column type, 0 rows, invalid target value (Float64/null in classification, null/non-finite in regression) Error::Runtime outputs.len() != rows, non-object predictor output, missing prediction, type mismatch in labels/positive, positive set on multiclass, single class without with.positive Error::Runtime probability present in only some rows, non-numeric, non-finite, or outside [0.0, 1.0] Error::Runtime Non-finite computed metric (e.g. overflow in regression) Error::Runtime Gate failed with on_fail: fail Error::Block Cancellation via ctx.cancel() Error::Cancelled

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• In-memory test set: the entire test Parquet artifact is loaded into memory and sent in a single predict_batch call.
  • Cancellation during predict_batch: ctx.cancel() is checked at run start, after fetching inputs, and after predict_batch, but does not interrupt an in-flight predict_batch call. For ExternalPythonPredictor, in-flight calls are already bounded by the worker's per-request timeout (default 30 s).
  • No production-model comparison in v0.1: comparing metrics against the current production model in a registry is planned for v0.2 (SPEC §3.6).
  • Shared standard PredictorRegistry in v0.1: register_std builds a single PredictorRegistry with register_std_predictors and shares it between both evaluate blocks; injecting custom predictors from library code is out of scope for v0.1.

docs.title: std/external
docs.text:
Runs any command (Python, R, Julia, a container…) as a pipeline step — custom preprocessing, feature engineering, model training, custom evaluation metrics, report generation, or anything else. Behind the optional external Cargo feature of mallops-std (Stage::Custom, version 0.1.0).

mallops materializes the input artifacts into a working directory, writes inputs.json and config.json, runs the command, and commits what the command declares in outputs.json. No Rust bindings are needed. See SPEC FR-PRE-2, FR-TRN-3, FR-EVL-3 and ADR-0003.

Generic example (custom feature engineering emitting features and metrics):

blocks:
  custom_features:
    use: std/external
    in: { dataset: raw.dataset }
    with:
      command: ["python", "./featurize.py"]
      inputs: { dataset: dataset }
      outputs: { features: features, metrics: metrics }
      params: { window: 7 }

Training example (emitting a model artifact with a flavor):

blocks:
  model:
    use: std/external
    in: { train: features.train }
    with:
      command: ["python", "./train.py"]
      inputs: { train: features }
      outputs: { model: model }
      flavor: sklearn-pickle
      params: { n_estimators: 200 }
      secrets: [MLFLOW_TOKEN]
      timeout_secs: 3600

A runnable reference script is in examples/external/train.py.

docs.title: Configuration (with:)
docs.text:
Unknown fields are rejected.

Field Type Default Meaning command list of strings required argv, executed directly (never through a shell). Not empty; command[0] not empty. inputs map port → kind required Declared input ports (may be {}). Every declared port is required. outputs map port → kind required Declared output ports (must be non-empty). Every declared port is required. flavor string none Allowed only when at least one declared port has kind model. Sets the flavor of every port of kind model (inputs and outputs); fills model outputs that do not set their own. params object {} Free-form, written to config.json. env list of names [] Host environment variables passed to the child; names unset on the host are skipped. secrets list of names [] Resolved with ctx.secret(name) and passed as env vars of the same name. timeout_secs integer > 0 none (no timeout) Kill the process group after this many seconds. log_cap_bytes integer > 0 1 MiB Max bytes kept per stream (stdout, stderr); the rest is drained and dropped. watch_files list of paths [] Files that make the block cacheable (see Cache).

Validation (mallops validate, which never runs the command):

  • inputs and outputs are required; outputs must declare at least one port (inputs may be empty {}).
  • Port names match [a-z][a-z0-9_]* (also re-checked at run time for input names given through the library API).
  • flavor is rejected unless at least one declared input or output port has kind model.
  • env / secrets names match [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*, are disjoint from each other and differ from PATH, SYSTEMROOT and MALLOPS_*.
  • Strings containing ${secret: in command, flavor, params, env, secrets or watch_files are rejected: use secrets:.

docs.title: Ports
docs.text:
std/external has no default ports: inputs and outputs must always be declared explicitly in with: (and are resolved dynamically via Block::resolve_ports).

  • outputs must contain at least one port; inputs may be empty.
  • Every declared input and output port is required (there are no optional ports).
  • When flavor is set, it applies to every declared port of kind model (inputs and outputs).
  • Unknown ports, kind mismatches and missing required outputs are checked by the runtime when it commits the outputs.

docs.title: Contract v1
docs.text:
mallops runs the command with the node workdir as cwd (mode 0700 on Unix; removed with the run). Every contract file carries "protocol_version": 1; a command must refuse any other value.

<workdir>/
  inputs.json        written by mallops
  config.json        written by mallops
  inputs/<port>/…    read-only copies of the input files
  outputs.json       written by the command
  …                  whatever the command writes (outputs live here)

Input files are materialized read-only (directories stay writable) and made writable again when the node ends, whatever the outcome, so the run workdir can be removed (Windows refuses to delete read-only files). All paths in the contract use / and are relative to the workdir.

docs.title: inputs.json
docs.text:
{
  "protocol_version": 1,
  "inputs": {
    "train": {
      "id": "<artifact id, hex>",
      "path": "inputs/train",
      "manifest": {
        "schema_version": 1,
        "kind": "features",
        "format": "parquet",
        "metadata": {},
        "parents": []
      }
    }
  }
}

inputs contains an entry for every declared input port (or {} when with.inputs is empty). manifest is the artifact manifest; flavor and io_schema appear only when set.

{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["protocol_version", "inputs"],
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "protocol_version": { "const": 1 },
    "inputs": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": {
        "type": "object",
        "required": ["id", "path", "manifest"],
        "additionalProperties": false,
        "properties": {
          "id": { "type": "string" },
          "path": { "type": "string" },
          "manifest": { "type": "object" }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: config.json
docs.text:
{
  "protocol_version": 1,
  "flavor": "sklearn-pickle",
  "params": { "n_estimators": 200 },
  "run_id": "<run id>"
}

flavor is null when not configured; params is {} when absent. Secrets are never written here.

{
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["protocol_version", "flavor", "params", "run_id"],
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "protocol_version": { "const": 1 },
    "flavor": { "type": ["string", "null"] },
    "params": { "type": "object" },
    "run_id": { "type": "string" }
  }
}

docs.title: outputs.json
docs.text:
{
  "protocol_version": 1,
  "status": "produced",
  "outputs": {
    "model": {
      "path": "out/model.pkl",
      "kind": "model",
      "format": "pickle",
      "flavor": "sklearn-pickle",
      "io_schema": null,
      "metadata": { "n_estimators": 200 }
    }
  }
}

status is "produced" or "skipped"; a skip may carry "skip_reason": "…" and no outputs. Per output: path and kind and format are required; flavor, io_schema and metadata are optional. An explicit flavor is accepted on any port; when absent, outputs of kind model get the configured with.flavor.

{
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["protocol_version", "status"],
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "protocol_version": { "const": 1 },
    "status": { "enum": ["produced", "skipped"] },
    "skip_reason": { "type": ["string", "null"] },
    "outputs": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": {
        "type": "object",
        "required": ["path", "kind", "format"],
        "additionalProperties": false,
        "properties": {
          "path": { "type": "string" },
          "kind": { "enum": ["dataset", "features", "transform", "model", "metrics", "package", "blob"] },
          "format": { "type": "string" },
          "flavor": { "type": ["string", "null"] },
          "io_schema": {},
          "metadata": { "type": "object" }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

mallops validates each path: it must be a valid relative path (no .., not absolute), no component under the workdir may be a symlink, its canonical path must stay inside the workdir, and it must be a regular file (committed as a file artifact) or a directory (committed as a directory artifact). A non-zero exit is an error even if outputs.json exists.

docs.title: Environment of the child
docs.text:
The inherited environment is cleared. The child always gets:

  • PATH (and SYSTEMROOT on Windows),
  • MALLOPS_PIPELINE_DIR: mallops' current directory, absolute (the directory of mallops.yaml: the CLI changes into it),
  • the host variables listed in env that are set on the host (unset ones are skipped), and the secrets (same name as in the config).

Nothing else leaks in: list what you need (HOME, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, VIRTUAL_ENV…).

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text: Declare names in secrets:; the value comes from ctx.secret(name) and reaches the child only as an environment variable. It never appears in config.json, the cache key or lineage, and its value is redacted from captured stdout/stderr (including the stderr tail in error messages).

docs.title: Relative paths in command
docs.text: The child's cwd is the workdir, so a relative script path would not resolve. Every command argument starting with ./ or ../ is made absolute against mallops' current directory (the mallops.yaml directory when run from the CLI). Bare words (python, train.py, -m) are left unchanged and looked up through PATH. Hence ["python", "./train.py"], not ["python", "train.py"].

docs.title: Cache
docs.text:
• Without watch_files the block is uncacheable: it runs every time.
  • With watch_files it is cacheable: the key adds a domain-separated BLAKE3 hash (mallops/external/watch_files/v1) of every watched file's path and content, in a fixed order. A missing file or a directory is an error.

Not part of the key: values of host environment variables, the binary or interpreter, and the Python (or other) dependencies. Add the script and a lock file to watch_files, and change params when you bump the environment.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Situation Error Missing inputs or outputs, empty outputs, flavor without any model port, invalid port / env / secrets name, ${secret: in config, unknown field Error::Config (reported under blocks.<id>.with by mallops validate) Timeout Error::Runtime("timed out after Ns"), process group killed Cancellation Error::Cancelled, process group killed Non-zero exit or killed by signal Error::Runtime with the tail of stderr (secrets redacted) Missing/malformed outputs.json, wrong protocol_version, bad path or symlink Error::Runtime naming the problem Unknown port, wrong kind, missing required output rejected when the runtime commits outputs

docs.title: Security
docs.text: The command is trusted code that runs with your user's privileges; this is not a sandbox (ADR-0007 D7, mallops.yaml is trusted). Process-group kill, a cleared environment and read-only inputs are guard rails against accidents, not isolation. Flavors that execute code on load (e.g. sklearn-pickle, joblib, torchscript) additionally require an explicit opt-in to be served. mallops validate never launches the command.

docs.title: What mallops does not manage
docs.text:
Python itself, interpreter versions, virtualenvs, dependencies and containers are yours. Point command at the interpreter you want (["./.venv/bin/python", "./train.py"]), or use a container:

command: ["docker", "run", "--rm", "-e", "MLFLOW_TOKEN", "my-runner:1.2"]
secrets: [MLFLOW_TOKEN]

Forward env vars explicitly with -e NAME. The container only sees the workdir (inputs, contract files, outputs) if you mount it, and its path is not known statically: use a small wrapper script (["./run-in-docker.sh"]) that runs docker run -v "$PWD:/work" -w /work ….

docs.title: Platform notes
docs.text:
• Library use: the block spawns processes and timers, so the host needs a tokio runtime built with enable_all().
  • Windows: only the direct child is killed on timeout or cancellation; there is no process-group kill, so grandchildren may survive. On Unix the whole group is killed.

docs.title: std/package
docs.text:
Model packaging block that bundles a trained model, an optional fitted preprocessing transform, and optional evaluation metrics into a self-contained package artifact (format: dir). Behind the optional package Cargo feature of mallops-std (package = [], not in default, no new crate dependency; enabled in mallops-cli). See SPEC FR-PKG-1.

blocks:
  package:
    use: std/package
    in:
      model: model.model
      preprocess: features.transform
      metrics: eval.metrics

preprocess and metrics are optional; a minimal model-only package wires only model:

blocks:
  package:
    use: std/package
    in: { model: model.model }

docs.title: Configuration (with:)
docs.text: std/package takes no configuration. with: must be omitted or an empty mapping ({}). Any non-empty value — including unknown keys, non-object values, or ${secret: references — is rejected with Error::Config by both validate_config (caught by mallops validate under blocks.<id>.with) and run.

docs.title: Ports
docs.text:
version: "0.1.0", Stage::Package:

  • Block ID: std/package
  • Inputs:
  • model (required): kind: model, any format, any flavor (the model manifest must carry a flavor at runtime).
  • preprocess (optional): kind: transform, any format.
  • metrics (optional): kind: metrics, any format.
  • Output:
  • package: kind: package, format: dir.

docs.title: Execution and directory layout
docs.text:
• Quality gate check: if metrics is wired and metrics.manifest().metadata["gate"]["passed"] == false (for example, from std/evaluate with on_fail: skip), std/package does not bundle the model and returns BlockOutcome::Skipped { reason: "metrics gate failed", outputs: OutputDrafts::new() }. Because the node is Skipped, it is never cached and mallops run leaves runs/latest.json unchanged so mallops serve keeps serving the previous accepted package. When metrics is omitted, no gate check is performed.
  • Materialization: each present input is materialized into <workdir>/package/ via store.fetch (package/model/, optional package/transform/, optional package/metrics/). store.fetch rejects symlinks and validates relative paths via RelPath; the runtime re-validates the resulting DraftPayload::Dir on commit.
  • Directory layout (payload/):
payload/
├── package.json
├── model/…          # materialized model artifact payload
├── transform/…      # optional: materialized preprocess artifact payload
└── metrics/…        # optional: materialized metrics artifact payload
  • Cancellation: ctx.cancel() is checked at run start and after each store.fetch.

docs.title: package.json format
docs.text:
package.json is compact deterministic JSON serialized from a struct with fixed field order, with no timestamps or run IDs:

{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "flavor": "smartcore-logistic",
  "io_schema": {
    "input": [{ "name": "age", "type": "f64" }],
    "output": [{ "name": "churned", "type": "bool" }]
  },
  "model": {
    "path": "model",
    "id": "<64-hex-artifact-id>",
    "manifest": { "...": "embedded model Manifest" }
  },
  "transform": {
    "path": "transform",
    "id": "<64-hex-artifact-id>",
    "manifest": { "...": "embedded transform Manifest" }
  },
  "metrics": {
    "path": "metrics",
    "id": "<64-hex-artifact-id>",
    "manifest": { "...": "embedded metrics Manifest" }
  }
}
  • schema_version: always 1.
  • flavor: model flavor string, matching the package manifest's flavor.
  • io_schema: omitted when absent; when present, matches the package manifest's io_schema.
  • model (required), transform (optional), metrics (optional): each entry carries its fixed relative path ("model", "transform", "metrics"), its source ArtifactId (id), and its embedded source Manifest (manifest).
  • Embedding the source manifests makes the package self-contained: downstream consumers (mallops serve, std/predict.batch) reconstruct the model's Artifact for Predictor::load from the package ArtifactId alone, without requiring the original source artifacts to remain in the store.

docs.title: Output manifest (flavor and io_schema)
docs.text:
Output manifest fields:

  • kind: package
  • format: dir
  • flavor: propagated from model.manifest().flavor. If model has no flavor, the block fails with Error::Runtime (an unflavored model cannot be dispatched to a Predictor at serve time).
  • io_schema:
  • Without preprocess: copied from model.manifest().io_schema (omitted if model has no io_schema, e.g. opaque models from std/external).
  • With preprocess: composed as { "input": <raw_input>, "output": model.io_schema.output }, where <raw_input> is transform.io_schema.input with any column whose name appears in model.io_schema.output removed (so the target column is excluded from the serving input schema). If either preprocess or model lacks io_schema, the package's io_schema is omitted.
  • Coherence check: when both transform.io_schema.output and model.io_schema.input are present, every { "name", "type" } column in model.io_schema.input must appear in transform.io_schema.output with matching name and type; otherwise the block fails with Error::Runtime at package time instead of failing later at serve time.
  • metadata: empty ({}). No timestamps, run IDs, or block-written parents (the runtime injects parents on commit).

docs.title: Cache
docs.text:
CachePolicy::Deterministic { extra_hash: None }.

  • Identical inputs, config, node seed:, and block version hit the cache and produce the same canonical ArtifactId, independent of the node workdir path.
  • Skipped runs (such as a failed metrics gate) are never cached.

docs.title: Loading packages (mallops_std::Package)
docs.text:
When the package feature is enabled, mallops-std re-exports mallops_std::Package for consumers such as mallops serve and std/predict.batch:

impl Package {
    pub async fn load(
        store: &dyn ArtifactStore,
        id: &ArtifactId,
        dest: &Path,
    ) -> Result<Package, Error>;

    pub fn model(&self) -> &Artifact;
    pub fn model_dir(&self) -> PathBuf;
    pub fn transform(&self) -> Option<(&Artifact, PathBuf)>;
    pub fn flavor(&self) -> &str;
    pub fn io_schema(&self) -> Option<&serde_json::Value>;
}

The future returned by Package::load is Send. Callers inside a Block can pass ctx.store().as_ref().

docs.title: What Package::load verifies
docs.text:
1. Integrity verification: calls store.verify(id) first. Because the canonical ArtifactId hashes manifest.json, package.json and every bundled payload file, any tampering or corruption in the store fails with Error::Store. An absent id is Error::Config.
  2. Manifest check: store.get(id); kind must be package and format "dir", otherwise Error::Config.
  3. Materialization: fetches the package directory into dest via store.fetch(id, dest).
  4. Descriptor validation (Error::Runtime on any failure): parses dest/package.json with deny_unknown_fields and checks:
  5. schema_version == 1
  6. flavor equals the package manifest's flavor (which must be present), and the embedded model manifest's flavor
  7. io_schema equals the package manifest's io_schema (null counts as absent)
  8. model.path == "model", transform.path == "transform" (if present), and metrics.path == "metrics" (if present)
  9. embedded manifest kinds match (Model, Transform, Metrics) and their schema_version is the supported one
  10. model/ (and transform/ when present) exist inside dest.

docs.title: Trust policy
docs.text: Package::load verifies store integrity and structural consistency, but does not enforce model code-execution trust policy. That policy belongs to the consumer: callers must resolve the predictor through PredictorRegistry::get(pkg.flavor(), trust_unsafe_flavors) before calling predictor.load(pkg.model(), pkg.model_dir()).

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Situation Error Non-empty with: (any key, non-object value, ${secret: reference) Error::Config (in mallops validate, aggregated into Error::Validation under blocks.<id>.with) Missing flavor in model manifest Error::Runtime model.io_schema.input column missing from or incompatible with transform.io_schema.output Error::Runtime Cancellation via ctx.cancel() Error::Cancelled Package::load: artifact id not found in store, kind != package or format != dir Error::Config Package::load: store corruption or tampering detected by store.verify(id) Error::Store Package::load: missing manifest flavor, invalid package.json, unsupported schema_version (descriptor or embedded manifest), mismatched flavor/io_schema/path/embedded kind, or missing bundled subdir Error::Runtime

A wired metrics input with metadata["gate"]["passed"] == false is not an error: std/package returns BlockOutcome::Skipped { reason: "metrics gate failed" }.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• Coherence check scope: the io_schema check compares {name, type} of columns only; other column fields are ignored.
  • No trust policy in Package: see Trust policy.
  • No environment requirements in v0.1: recording runtime/Python dependency requirements in the package descriptor is deferred to a later release (SPEC FR-PKG-1).
  • No OCI packaging or signing in v0.1: OCI image output (FR-PKG-2, v0.2) and cryptographic signing (FR-PKG-3, v0.3) are out of scope for v0.1.

docs.title: Predictor contract
docs.text:
The Predictor contract (ADR-0007 D6/D7) turns a model artifact into an active inference component that answers prediction requests. mallops-core remains strictly model-agnostic and free of machine learning dependencies; consumers pick a Predictor by the artifact's flavor via a local PredictorRegistry.

In v0.1, the minimal contract lives in mallops-std (shared by evaluate and serve) before its promotion to mallops-core ahead of 1.0.

See SPEC FR-SRV-3 and ARCHITECTURE §7 Serving.

docs.title: Cargo features
docs.text:
All predictor components in mallops-std are opt-in (not in default):

Feature Dependencies What it enables predictor mallops-core, serde, serde_json, tokio Base types (PredictInput, Predictor, LoadedPredictor), PredictorRegistry, register_std_predictors, and the conformance suite conformance::check. predict-smartcore predictor SmartcorePredictor for smartcore-logistic and smartcore-linear. Evaluates models in-process without depending on the smartcore crate. predict-external predictor, tokio/process, tokio/io-util, tokio/time ExternalPythonPredictor for sklearn-pickle. Evaluates models via an external Python worker subprocess communicating over NDJSON v1.

docs.title: PredictInput
docs.text:
Prediction request and response payloads:

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum PredictInput {
    /// A JSON document.
    Json(serde_json::Value),
    /// Opaque bytes with their media type.
    Bytes {
        /// Media type of `data`.
        content_type: String,
        /// The raw payload.
        data: Vec<u8>,
    },
}
  • PredictInput::Json wraps any serde_json::Value (objects, numbers, arrays).
  • PredictInput::Bytes carries unparsed raw payloads with an explicit MIME content_type.
  • Marked #[non_exhaustive] to allow future zero-copy buffer variants.

docs.title: Predictor
docs.text:
Factory trait that loads model artifacts for one or more flavor identifiers:

pub trait Predictor: Send + Sync {
    /// The artifact `flavor` values this predictor can load (non-empty).
    fn flavors(&self) -> &[&str];

    /// Whether loading a model runs code shipped in the artifact (pickle, joblib, …).
    /// Such predictors are refused by [`PredictorRegistry::get`] unless trust is given.
    fn executes_code(&self) -> bool;

    /// Loads the model whose payload files are in `payload_dir`.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Any [`Error`] if the payload is missing or malformed.
    fn load<'a>(
        &'a self,
        artifact: &'a Artifact,
        payload_dir: &'a Path,
    ) -> BoxFuture<'a, Result<Box<dyn LoadedPredictor>, Error>>;
}
  • flavors(): slice of supported artifact flavor strings (must not be empty).
  • executes_code(): returns true if loading the model executes code contained in the artifact (e.g., Python pickle / joblib). Governed by the trust model.
  • load(&'a self, artifact: &'a Artifact, payload_dir: &'a Path): loads the model from files in payload_dir against artifact.manifest(). Returns an asynchronous BoxFuture resolving to a trait object Box<dyn LoadedPredictor>.

docs.title: LoadedPredictor
docs.text:
A model instantiated in memory, ready to answer inference requests:

pub trait LoadedPredictor: Send + Sync {
    /// Predicts one input.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Any [`Error`] if the input is malformed or the model fails.
    fn predict(&self, input: PredictInput) -> BoxFuture<'_, Result<PredictInput, Error>>;

    /// Predicts a batch; outputs are in input order.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Any [`Error`] if any input is malformed or the model fails.
    fn predict_batch(
        &self,
        inputs: Vec<PredictInput>,
    ) -> BoxFuture<'_, Result<Vec<PredictInput>, Error>>;
}
  • predict: answers a single prediction request.
  • predict_batch: answers multiple prediction requests. The output vector must strictly match the length and order of inputs. Passing an empty Vec must succeed and return an empty Vec.

docs.title: PredictorRegistry
docs.text:
PredictorRegistry resolves predictors by artifact flavor. It is an explicit local instance (no global state, no linker magic).

let mut registry = PredictorRegistry::new();
register_std_predictors(&mut registry)?;

// Resolving a predictor:
let predictor = registry.get("smartcore-logistic", false)?;
let loaded = predictor.load(&artifact, payload_dir).await?;

docs.title: Registration: register
docs.text:
pub fn register(&mut self, predictor: Arc<dyn Predictor>) -> Result<(), Error>

Registers predictor for all its declared flavors atomically.

  • If predictor.flavors() is empty, returns Error::Validation ("predictor declares no flavors").
  • If flavors() contains duplicate entries, or if any flavor is already registered, returns Error::Validation ("duplicate predictor flavor <flavor>").
  • Atomic rollback: if any flavor conflicts, the registry is left completely unmodified.

docs.title: Resolution: get
docs.text:
pub fn get(&self, flavor: &str, trust_unsafe_flavors: bool) -> Result<Arc<dyn Predictor>, Error>

Retrieves the predictor registered for flavor, enforcing the code-execution trust policy:

  • If no predictor handles flavor: returns Error::Config("no predictor for flavor").
  • If predictor.executes_code() is true and trust_unsafe_flavors is false: returns Error::Config("flavorexecutes code from the artifact; pass --trust-unsafe-flavors to serve it").

docs.title: Standard predictors: register_std_predictors
docs.text:
pub fn register_std_predictors(registry: &mut PredictorRegistry) -> Result<(), Error>

Registers all standard predictors enabled by active Cargo feature flags:

  • SmartcorePredictor when predict-smartcore is enabled (smartcore-logistic, smartcore-linear).
  • ExternalPythonPredictor when predict-external is enabled (sklearn-pickle).

Fails with Error::Validation if a standard flavor is already present in registry.

docs.title: Conformance suite (conformance::check)
docs.text:
mallops_std::predictor::conformance::check is a reusable compliance test suite for any Predictor implementation:

pub async fn check(
    predictor: &dyn Predictor,
    artifact: &Artifact,
    payload_dir: &Path,
    cases: &[(PredictInput, PredictInput)],
    malformed: PredictInput,
) -> Result<(), String>

It validates compliance without panicking, returning Err(String) on the first rule violation:

  1. Flavor advertisement: if artifact.manifest().flavor is Some(flavor), checks that predictor.flavors() contains flavor.
  2. Model loading: calls predictor.load(artifact, payload_dir).await and verifies success.
  3. Single prediction correctness: evaluates each (input, expected) pair in cases via loaded.predict(input) and confirms got == expected.
  4. Batch prediction preservation: evaluates loaded.predict_batch(cases.inputs) and verifies that outputs match expected in exact input order.
  5. Empty batch handling: evaluates loaded.predict_batch(vec![]) and verifies that it returns an empty Vec.
  6. Error handling: verifies that loaded.predict(malformed) returns an Err.

docs.title: SmartcorePredictor
docs.text:
Feature: predict-smartcore. Serves models trained by std/train.smartcore in-process without linking to smartcore (pure Rust, no BLAS, zero unsafe code).

  • Flavors: smartcore-logistic, smartcore-linear
  • executes_code(): false (safe data format, permitted by default without --trust-unsafe-flavors)

docs.title: Load validation rules
docs.text:
During load(artifact, payload_dir), SmartcorePredictor performs exhaustive validation:

  1. Artifact kind: artifact.manifest().kind must be ArtifactKind::Model.
  2. Artifact format: artifact.manifest().format must be "json".
  3. Artifact flavor: artifact.manifest().flavor must be present and match one of smartcore-logistic or smartcore-linear.
  4. Payload file: payload_dir/model.json must exist, be valid JSON, and reject unknown fields (deny_unknown_fields).
  5. Schema version: v must equal 1 (MODEL_SCHEMA_VERSION).
  6. Flavor & algorithm alignment:
  7. smartcore-logistic requires algorithm: "logistic_regression".
  8. smartcore-linear requires algorithm: "linear_regression".
  9. Any mismatch fails with an error.
  10. Features: features list must be non-empty and must not contain duplicate feature names.
  11. Target: target column name must not be empty.
  12. Coefficients: coefficients.len() must equal features.len(), and all coefficients must be finite floating-point numbers.
  13. Intercept: intercept must be a finite floating-point number.
  14. Algorithm-specific fields:
    • For logistic_regression:
    • classes is required and must contain exactly 2 distinct classes (int64, bool, or string).
    • threshold is required and must be a finite floating-point number.
    • For linear_regression:
    • classes and threshold must be omitted (null / absent).

docs.title: Input and output shapes
docs.text:
• Input: PredictInput::Json containing a JSON object.
  • The object keys must match model.json's features list exactly (missing or extra keys are rejected).
  • Each value must be a finite JSON number or a boolean (true maps to 1.0, false maps to 0.0).
  • Non-object JSON and PredictInput::Bytes are rejected with Error::Runtime.
  • Output (smartcore-logistic):
  • Returns PredictInput::Json with shape: 
    {
  "prediction": <class>,
  "probability": <f64>
}
  • Probability calculation: p = 1.0 / (1.0 + exp(-(intercept + Σ coefficients[i] * x[i]))).
  • Prediction decision: classes[1] when p >= threshold, otherwise classes[0].
  • Preserves the original JSON type of classes (int64, bool, or string).
  • Output (smartcore-linear):
  • Returns PredictInput::Json with shape: 
    {
  "prediction": <f64>
}
  • Calculated as: prediction = intercept + Σ coefficients[i] * x[i].

docs.title: ExternalPythonPredictor
docs.text:
Feature: predict-external. Serves models through an external Python worker process speaking NDJSON protocol v1 over stdin/stdout.

  • Flavors: sklearn-pickle
  • executes_code(): true (unpickling arbitrary models executes arbitrary code; requires explicit --trust-unsafe-flavors opt-in)

docs.title: Command and configuration
docs.text:
• Default command: runs the embedded reference worker (worker.py) directly with Python:
  • Unix: ["python3", "-c", "<worker.py>"]
  • Windows: ["python", "-c", "<worker.py>"]
  • with_command(Vec<String>): overrides worker command arguments (executed directly, never through a shell).
  • with_timeout(Duration): sets per-request and handshake timeout (default: 30 seconds).

docs.title: Model file selection
docs.text:
During load, ExternalPythonPredictor locates the model file inside payload_dir:

  1. Uses payload_dir/model.pkl if it exists.
  2. If model.pkl is absent, searches payload_dir for regular files (subdirectories are ignored). If there is exactly one regular file (e.g. model.joblib), it is selected.
  3. If payload_dir has 0 files or more than 1 file without model.pkl, loading fails with Error::Runtime.

docs.title: Worker environment and directory hygiene
docs.text:
The worker child process is spawned with an isolated environment and working directory:

  • Working directory: set to payload_dir (resolved via std::path::absolute without UNC \\?\ prefix on Windows to avoid Python import path confusion).
  • Environment isolation: host environment is completely cleared (env_clear). The worker inherits only:
  • PATH (plus SYSTEMROOT on Windows).
  • MALLOPS_MODEL_FILE: absolute path to the resolved model file.
  • MALLOPS_FEATURES: JSON array string of feature names extracted in order from artifact.manifest().io_schema.input[*].name (omitted if empty or absent).
  • sys.path hygiene: on startup, worker.py purges '' (the cwd) and the absolute payload path from sys.path before any other imports. This prevents untrusted payload files from shadowing standard Python modules (such as a malicious json.py or pickle.py).
  • Stream separation: worker.py immediately redirects sys.stdout = sys.stderr. All user/model print statements go to stderr, keeping stdout clean for the NDJSON protocol.
  • Stderr ring buffer: an asynchronous background task drains the worker's stderr, keeping the most recent 4 KiB (STDERR_TAIL). If the worker crashes or closes its pipes, the task drains stderr for up to 1 second (STDERR_DRAIN), and the tail is included in Error::Runtime.
  • Protocol line limit: protocol lines are bounded by 64 MiB (MAX_LINE = 64 << 20). Exceeding this limit triggers a protocol violation error.

docs.title: NDJSON Protocol v1
docs.text: Communication occurs over standard streams with one UTF-8 JSON object per line (\n terminated):

docs.title: 1. Handshake
docs.text:
Upon loading the model into memory, the worker writes:

{"v": 1, "type": "ready"}

The host must receive this within the configured timeout (default 30 s).

docs.title: 2. Single prediction (predict)
docs.text:
Host request:

{"id": 0, "type": "predict", "input": {"age": 42.0, "plan_a": 1.0}}

Worker success response:

{"id": 0, "ok": true, "output": {"prediction": 1, "probability": 0.875}}

docs.title: 3. Batch prediction (predict_batch)
docs.text:
Host request:

{"id": 1, "type": "predict_batch", "inputs": [{"age": 25.0, "plan_a": 0.0}, {"age": 50.0, "plan_a": 1.0}]}

Worker success response:

{"id": 1, "ok": true, "outputs": [{"prediction": 0, "probability": 0.12}, {"prediction": 1, "probability": 0.91}]}

docs.title: 4. Error response
docs.text:
If a prediction fails (e.g. missing features or invalid input):

Worker error response:

{"id": 2, "ok": false, "error": "ValueError: missing features ['plan_a']"}

The host maps this to Error::Runtime("worker error: ValueError: missing features ['plan_a']"). A single failed request does not crash or terminate the worker.

docs.title: Input & output representations
docs.text:
• Inputs: worker.py accepts either an object {"feature": value} (ordered using MALLOPS_FEATURES or the model's feature_names_in_) or a list of values already in column order.
  • Outputs: {"prediction": <val>}. If the model provides predict_proba and has exactly two classes (len(classes_) == 2), "probability": <p> is included — the probability of the greater class (classes[1] in sorted ascending order, matching scikit-learn's classes_[1] and SmartcorePredictor). Consumers such as std/evaluate.classification rely on this contract to compute roc_auc (using 1 - p when with.positive is classes[0]).
  • NumPy scalars and arrays are automatically converted to standard JSON primitives via .tolist() / .item().

docs.title: Lifecycle, failure recovery, and process management
docs.text:
• Serialized requests: inference requests are serialized through an asynchronous Mutex.
  • Failure recovery: if a request times out, receives an invalid reply, finds the worker dead, or if the request future is cancelled/dropped mid-flight, the worker process is killed (kill_on_drop(true)). The worker slot is vacated.
  • Automatic restart: on the subsequent request, a fresh worker child process is spawned automatically. The failed request itself is not retried.
  • Drop cleanup: dropping LoadedPredictor drops the active worker child process, killing it immediately.
  • Platform note (Windows): process termination on drop or crash terminates only the direct child process. There is no process-group kill on Windows, so Python workers must not spawn detached subprocesses.
