docs.title: mallops serve
docs.text:
HTTP/JSON inference server that serves a self-contained package artifact produced by mallops run (std/package). Serving runs as a native process (mallops binary) outside the batch DAG; container packaging (FR-PKG-2) and Docker/Kubernetes deploy targets (FR-DEP-1) are deferred to v0.2. Flavors backed by ExternalPythonPredictor (sklearn-pickle) spawn a local Python worker subprocess, not a container.

In mallops-std, the HTTP server lives in mallops_std::serve behind the optional serve-http Cargo feature (not in default; enabled in mallops-cli). See SPEC FR-SRV-1, ARCHITECTURE §7, and the Predictor contract.

docs.title: CLI usage and configuration
docs.text:
mallops serve [PACKAGE_ID] \
  [--host <HOST>] \
  [--port <PORT>] \
  [--trust-unsafe-flavors] \
  [--max-body-bytes <N>] \
  [--timeout <SECS>] \
  [--max-concurrency <N>] \
  [--auth-token-secret <NAME>]

Global flags (-f / --file <PATH>, default mallops.yaml; -v / --verbose) apply as usual. Unlike other subcommands (which default to WARN), mallops serve initializes stderr logging at INFO so per-request metadata logs are visible by default (-v raises the level to DEBUG).

docs.title: Precedence and defaults
docs.text:
Configuration is resolved with precedence:

CLI flags > serve: in mallops.yaml > defaults

The top-level serve: section of mallops.yaml supports package, host, and port:

serve:
  package: package.package
  host: 127.0.0.1
  port: 8080
Setting CLI flag mallops.yaml Default Bind host --host <HOST> serve.host 127.0.0.1 Bind port --port <PORT> serve.port 8080 (0 = OS-assigned) Max request body --max-body-bytes <N> — 10485760 (10 MiB) Request timeout --timeout <SECS> — 30 s Max concurrent requests --max-concurrency <N> — 64 Allow code-executing flavors --trust-unsafe-flavors — false Bearer auth secret name --auth-token-secret <NAME> — none (unauthenticated)

docs.title: Package resolution and store requirement
docs.text:
• Without PACKAGE_ID: requires a serve: section in mallops.yaml and a runs/latest.json record in the store whose pipeline matches name in mallops.yaml. The server resolves serve.package (<block>.<port>) from latest.json's outputs. If no matching successful run exists, startup fails with: 
    error: no successful run: run `mallops run` first
  • With explicit PACKAGE_ID: loads that ArtifactId directly from the store configured in mallops.yaml. mallops.yaml is still required to locate and open the store.
  • Persistent store required: mallops serve requires a persistent store (store.kind: local in v0.1). Configuring store.kind: memory fails with: 
    error: serve needs a persistent store

docs.title: Startup and shutdown
docs.text:
• Once the package and predictor are loaded and the listener is bound, the CLI prints: 
    serving <artifact-id> on http://<addr>
  • Graceful shutdown is triggered by Ctrl-C (SIGINT) on all platforms and SIGTERM on Unix. In-flight requests finish before the server drops the active LoadedPredictor (terminating any external Python worker) and removes its temporary package directory.

docs.title: GET /health
docs.text:
Liveness and readiness probe. Always unauthenticated and exempt from the request timeout and concurrency limiter so health checks do not fail with 503 when /predict is saturated.

Response (200 OK):

{
  "status": "ok",
  "package": "<64-hex-artifact-id>",
  "flavor": "smartcore-logistic"
}

After a hot-swap, package (and flavor) immediately report the newly active package.

docs.title: POST /predict
docs.text: Runs inference against the active package's optional fitted transform and Predictor.

docs.title: Request and response shapes
docs.text:
• Single input: a JSON object {...} returns a single JSON prediction object {...}: 
    curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/predict \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"age": 42, "tenure": 12}'

    {"prediction": 1, "probability": 0.87}
  • Batch input: a JSON array of objects [{...}, ...] returns a JSON array of predictions in the exact same order. An empty array [] returns 200 OK with []. 
    curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/predict \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '[{"age": 42, "tenure": 12}, {"age": 25, "tenure": 2}]'

    [{"prediction": 1, "probability": 0.87}, {"prediction": 0, "probability": 0.14}]

docs.title: Preprocessing pipeline
docs.text:
• Package with a bundled transform (transform.json): input rows (including a single object, wrapped as a 1-element array) are passed through FittedTransform::apply_json, converted to JSON row objects containing the columns declared in model.io_schema.input, and evaluated via LoadedPredictor::predict_batch. Loading a package that bundles a transform fails with Error::Config if mallops-std was compiled without the preprocess-tabular feature.
  • Package without a transform: rows are passed directly to the predictor.

docs.title: Middleware order
docs.text:
Every POST /predict request passes through the following layers in order:

  1. Metadata logging (tracing::info!)
  2. Request timeout (--timeout, returns 504)
  3. Bearer authentication (when configured, returns 401 before reading the body)
  4. Concurrency permit (--max-concurrency, returns 503 if saturated; held until response completion)
  5. Body size limit (--max-body-bytes, returns 413)
  6. JSON decode, transform, and prediction

docs.title: Status codes
docs.text:
All error responses — including 400 and 413 — are returned as JSON {"error": "<message>"}.

Status Meaning 200 OK Prediction succeeded (JSON object for single input, JSON array for batch input, [] for empty batch). 400 Bad Request Malformed JSON, payload is neither an object nor an array of objects, or fitted transform validation failed (apply_json). 401 Unauthorized Missing Authorization header, scheme other than Bearer, or invalid token. Includes WWW-Authenticate: Bearer and a generic error message. 413 Payload Too Large Request body exceeds --max-body-bytes (default 10 MiB). 500 Internal Server Error Predictor runtime error, or predictor returned non-JSON bytes (PredictInput::Bytes; the detail "non-JSON prediction" goes to the warn log only). The client always receives {"error":"prediction failed"}; the request body is never echoed. 503 Service Unavailable Concurrency limit (--max-concurrency, default 64) reached. 504 Gateway Timeout Request exceeded --timeout (default 30 s).

docs.title: Bearer authentication
docs.text:
Pass --auth-token-secret <NAME> to require Authorization: Bearer <token> on POST /predict.

  • The CLI reads the token from the MALLOPS_SECRET_<NAME> environment variable via EnvSecretProvider.
  • A missing environment variable fails at startup with Error::Secret; an empty or whitespace-only token fails with Error::Config.
  • The server hashes the token with BLAKE3 on load and retains only the blake3::Hash digest (not the raw Secret), comparing incoming tokens in constant time via blake3::Hash equality.
  • Missing header, non-Bearer scheme, and wrong token all return 401 Unauthorized with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer and the same generic error message.
  • GET /health remains unauthenticated for liveness/readiness probes.
  • The server binds to 127.0.0.1 by default. Whenever you bind to 0.0.0.0 or another non-loopback address, enable --auth-token-secret and terminate TLS at a reverse proxy.

docs.title: Code-executing model flavors (--trust-unsafe-flavors)
docs.text: Model formats that execute arbitrary code on deserialization (such as sklearn-pickle, where Predictor::executes_code() is true) are refused with Error::Config unless --trust-unsafe-flavors is explicitly passed. This trust gate is enforced both at startup and on every hot-swap. See SPEC §4.1 Trust model and PredictorRegistry::get.

docs.title: Request logging (metadata only)
docs.text:
Each POST /predict request emits a single structured tracing::info! event containing metadata only: method, path, status, latency_ms, req_bytes, and resp_bytes. GET /health and unknown routes are not logged.

  • Request and response bodies are never logged.
  • 4xx responses log only metadata (error details from JSON parsing or apply_json are not logged because they may contain input values).
  • 500 responses additionally log the internal predictor error at warn level (for external predictors, this may include the worker's stderr tail). Without a transform in the package, a predictor error may name a column sent by the client in that warn log (never the values).

docs.title: Retraining and hot-swap (SIGHUP)
docs.text:
Retraining with mallops run creates a new immutable package artifact (a new ArtifactId). runs/latest.json is updated only when every node in the pipeline reaches Succeeded — if a quality gate skips std/package or any node fails, runs/latest.json stays on the previous accepted package.

On Unix, sending SIGHUP (kill -HUP <pid>) reloads the server without dropping traffic:

# 1. Retrain and promote a new package (updates runs/latest.json only if all nodes succeed)
mallops run

# 2. Hot-swap the running server to the newly promoted package
kill -HUP <pid>

docs.title: Continuity guarantees
docs.text:
• Early signal installation: the CLI installs the SIGHUP handler before initial Server::load, so a signal arriving during startup never terminates the process.
  • Metadata-only reload: on SIGHUP, the CLI re-reads runs/latest.json from the store using the same pipeline name and serve.package reference configured at startup (mallops.yaml is not re-read) and calls ServeHandle::swap.
  • No-op on unchanged id: if the resolved ArtifactId matches the active package, swap returns Ok(false) without reloading.
  • Build before swap: the new state (Package::load into a fresh temporary directory, the --trust-unsafe-flavors gate, optional FittedTransform, and Predictor::load) is built completely before touching the active state.
  • Atomic swap & in-flight drain: the active Arc<State> is swapped atomically without holding a lock across .await. Requests already in flight finish on the previous state; the old predictor and its temporary directory are dropped only when the last in-flight request completes.
  • Serialized swaps: reloads are serialized through an async mutex so rapid SIGHUP signals do not load multiple packages concurrently.
  • Failure keeps the old package: if latest.json is unreadable, its pipeline does not match, or loading the new package fails (including trust gate rejection), a warning is emitted (a warning: ... line on stderr from the CLI for latest.json problems, a tracing warn from mallops-std for load and trust failures) and the server continues serving the previous package without interruption.
  • Schema change warning: if the new package has a different io_schema, the swap completes and logs a tracing warn (mallops-std).
  • Health update: GET /health immediately reports the new package id and flavor.

docs.title: Operational notes for SIGHUP
docs.text:
• Explicit PACKAGE_ID: when started as mallops serve <PACKAGE_ID>, the SIGHUP handler is still installed so the signal does not kill the server, but reloads are ignored with a warning: ... line on stderr.
  • Unix only: SIGHUP and SIGTERM handling exist only on Unix (#[cfg(unix)]). On Windows, only Ctrl-C is handled; reload requires restarting the process.
  • Stopping the server: because SIGHUP reloads instead of terminating on Unix, closing the controlling terminal (hangup) triggers a reload rather than exit. Always stop mallops serve with SIGTERM or Ctrl-C (SIGINT).
  • No /reload endpoint or polling in v0.1: remote reload endpoints and store polling are deferred to v0.3.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• Non-preemptive timeout for synchronous predictors: SmartcorePredictor evaluates in-process within a single poll, so tokio::time::timeout cannot preempt it mid-computation. If a large batch exceeds --timeout, the 504 is sent only after the computation finishes, and CPU-heavy batches can occupy a Tokio worker thread. Bound batch size with --max-body-bytes.
  • Serialized external worker: ExternalPythonPredictor serializes requests through an async mutex. Request timeouts work asynchronously on I/O, but timing out drops the request and kills the Python worker process, which restarts automatically on the next request.
  • Reverse proxy required in production: mallops serve speaks plain HTTP/1.1 without TLS, connection caps, or header-read timeouts. Deploy behind a reverse proxy (e.g. nginx, Caddy, Envoy) for TLS termination, connection limits, and protection against slow clients. When binding to 0.0.0.0, always configure --auth-token-secret.
  • No Docker/OCI in v0.1: mallops serve runs as a native process. OCI image packaging (FR-PKG-2) and Docker/Kubernetes deploy blocks (FR-DEP-1) are planned for v0.2.

docs.title: Rust API (mallops_std::serve)
docs.text:
Enabled by the serve-http Cargo feature of mallops-std:

use mallops_std::serve::{ServeHandle, ServeOptions, Server};

let mut opts = ServeOptions::default();
opts.max_concurrency = 64;

let server = Server::load(store.as_ref(), &package_id, &predictors, opts).await?;
let handle: ServeHandle = server.handle();

let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:8080").await?;
server.run(listener, shutdown_signal).await?;
  • ServeOptions (#[non_exhaustive], Default): holds host ("127.0.0.1"), port (8080), max_body_bytes (10 MiB), timeout (30 s), max_concurrency (64), trust_unsafe_flavors (false), and auth_token: Option<Secret> (None; an empty token fails with Error::Config). host and port are configuration values for callers/CLI; binding the TcpListener is the caller's responsibility.
  • Server::load(store, id, predictors, opts): verifies and materializes the package into a server-owned temporary directory via Package::load, enforces predictors.get(flavor, opts.trust_unsafe_flavors), and loads the optional FittedTransform and LoadedPredictor.
  • Server::handle(&self) -> ServeHandle: returns a cheaply Cloneable handle for hot-swaps.
  • Server::run(self, listener, shutdown): serves HTTP/1.1 on listener until shutdown resolves, drains in-flight requests, and drops the active state (predictor + temporary directory).
  • ServeHandle::swap(&self, store, id, predictors) -> Result<bool, Error>: atomically replaces the active package. Returns Ok(false) when id is already active, Ok(true) on a successful swap, or Err (logging a warn and leaving the active package unchanged).

docs.title: std/train.smartcore
docs.text:
Native classic machine-learning training block in Rust backed by smartcore 0.7 (pure Rust, Apache-2.0, no BLAS). Behind the optional train-smartcore Cargo feature of mallops-std (not in default). See SPEC FR-TRN-1.

blocks:
  model:
    use: std/train.smartcore
    in: { train: features.train }
    with:
      algorithm: logistic_regression
      target: churned
      seed: 42
      hyperparameters:
        alpha: 1.0

docs.title: Configuration (with:)
docs.text:
Unknown fields are rejected (deny_unknown_fields). validate_config uses the same parser as run, so mallops validate catches configuration errors before execution.

Field Type Default Meaning algorithm logistic_regression | linear_regression required Training algorithm (snake_case). target non-empty string none Target column name. Falls back to metadata["target"] of the train input artifact if omitted; if both are set and differ, the run fails. seed u64 none Optional seed recorded in the output manifest metadata. Neither v0.1 algorithm uses randomness; distinct from the node-level seed: (SPEC §5). hyperparameters object {} Algorithm-specific parameters (deserialized after algorithm; unknown keys rejected).

docs.title: hyperparameters by algorithm
docs.text:
logistic_regression (binary classification, fixed LBFGS solver):

Key Type Default Constraints alpha f64 1.0 Finite number >= 0.0.

linear_regression (ordinary least squares):

Key Type Default Constraints solver svd | qr svd Matrix factorization solver.

Validation rules:

  • Using a logistic_regression hyperparameter key with linear_regression, or vice versa, is an error.
  • Unknown algorithm or solver values, negative or non-finite alpha, and empty target are rejected.
  • Strings containing ${secret: anywhere in the config are rejected (as in std/external).

docs.title: Ports
docs.text:
• Input: train (required), kind: features, format: parquet.
  • Output: model, kind: model, format: json.
  • The static BlockSpec advertises both flavors: smartcore-logistic and smartcore-linear.
  • resolve_ports narrows the output flavor to the single flavor matching with.algorithm: smartcore-logistic for logistic_regression and smartcore-linear for linear_regression.

docs.title: Input data rules
docs.text:
• Target resolution: uses with.target when set, otherwise metadata["target"] (string) from the input artifact manifest. Missing in both is an error; present in both with different values is an error (with.target `<x>` differs from the input's metadata target `<y>`). The target column must exist in the Parquet schema.
  • Feature columns: every column other than the target, in the input schema's order. Allowed Arrow types are Boolean, Int64, and Float64 (cast to f64). Any other type fails with an error suggesting preprocessing with encode or select.
  • Values and shape:
  • Null values fail with an error naming the column.
  • Non-finite values (NaN, ±inf) fail with an error naming the column and row.
  • Empty datasets (0 rows) or datasets with no feature columns fail.
  • linear_regression requires rows >= features + 1.
  • Target types:
  • logistic_regression (binary only): Int64, Boolean, or Utf8 (Float64 is rejected). Distinct values are sorted (Int64 numerically, false < true for Boolean, byte order for Utf8). Anything other than 2 distinct classes fails. Internally the model fits on 0/1 labels (0 = classes[0], 1 = classes[1]), so positive coefficients correspond to classes[1].
  • linear_regression: Int64 or Float64 (cast to f64).
  • Post-fit checks and cancellation: non-finite intercepts or coefficients fail after fitting. A singular-matrix error from smartcore reports "features are linearly dependent (e.g. one_hot with all categories); drop a column". Cooperative cancellation (ctx.cancel()) is checked at run start, after fetching inputs, during Parquet reading, before and after fitting, and before writing the output; the fit itself is not interruptible.

docs.title: Model format (model.json)
docs.text:
The output artifact payload is a single file, model.json, serialized from a struct with fixed field order (no HashMap) and serde_json float formatting:

{
  "v": 1,
  "algorithm": "logistic_regression",
  "features": ["age", "plan_a"],
  "target": "churned",
  "intercept": -2.71,
  "coefficients": [1.11, -0.13],
  "classes": [false, true],
  "threshold": 0.5
}
  • classes and threshold are included only for logistic_regression and omitted for linear_regression.
  • classes keeps the JSON type of the target column: [0, 1] (int64), [false, true] (bool), or ["no", "yes"] (string), sorted ascending.

docs.title: Prediction rule
docs.text:
Implemented in-process by SmartcorePredictor without depending on smartcore:

  • logistic_regression: compute p = 1 / (1 + exp(-(intercept + Σ coefficients[i] * x[i]))); predict classes[1] when p >= threshold, otherwise classes[0].
  • linear_regression: compute y = intercept + Σ coefficients[i] * x[i].

docs.title: Manifest and io_schema
docs.text:
Output manifest fields:

  • kind: model
  • format: json
  • flavor: smartcore-logistic or smartcore-linear (pure data formats; do not execute code on load, allowed by default in mallops serve)
  • metadata:
  • algorithm: "logistic_regression" or "linear_regression"
  • hyperparameters: effective hyperparameters including defaults (e.g. {"alpha": 1.0} or {"solver": "svd"})
  • target: target column name
  • seed: present only when with.seed is configured
  • framework: "smartcore"
  • framework_version: "0.7"
  • No timestamps, run IDs, or block-written parents (the runtime injects parents on commit).

io_schema uses the same shape as the transform artifact from std/preprocess.tabular:

{
  "input": [
    { "name": "age", "type": "int64" },
    { "name": "plan_a", "type": "float64" }
  ],
  "output": [
    { "name": "churned", "type": "bool" }
  ]
}
  • input: feature columns with their original input types (bool, int64, or float64), in schema order.
  • output: single entry for the target column — original target type (int64, bool, or string) for logistic_regression, and float64 for linear_regression.

docs.title: Cache
docs.text:
CachePolicy::Deterministic { extra_hash: None }.

  • Same inputs, config, node seed:, and block version hit the cache and produce the same ArtifactId on the same machine.
  • Changing with.seed changes the manifest metadata and cache key, producing a different ArtifactId.
  • Upgrading smartcore or changing the model.json format requires bumping BlockSpec.version.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Situation Error Unknown field, invalid algorithm/solver, cross-algorithm hyperparameter key, negative or non-finite alpha, empty target, ${secret: in config Error::Config (in mallops validate, aggregated into Error::Validation under blocks.<id>.with) Missing target, with.target differing from input metadata["target"], or target absent from schema Error::Runtime naming the target Unsupported feature column type (not Boolean, Int64, or Float64) Error::Runtime suggesting encode/select in preprocess Null value in features or target Error::Runtime naming the column Non-finite (NaN/±inf) value Error::Runtime naming the column and row 0 rows, 0 features, or linear_regression with rows < features + 1 Error::Runtime logistic_regression with Float64 target or class count != 2 Error::Runtime linear_regression with target type other than Int64/Float64 Error::Runtime Collinear / singular feature matrix Error::Runtime ("features are linearly dependent (e.g. one_hot with all categories); drop a column") Non-finite intercept or coefficients after fit Error::Runtime Cancellation via ctx.cancel() Error::Cancelled

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• In-memory dense matrix: the entire training dataset is loaded into memory as a dense n × k f64 matrix.
  • Per-machine determinism: an identical ArtifactId is guaranteed on the same machine, not bit-for-bit across different CPUs or operating systems.
  • No convergence signal for logistic regression: LBFGS runs up to 1000 iterations and does not report non-convergence.
  • Binary logistic regression only: logistic_regression requires exactly 2 distinct target classes.

docs.title: Algorithms not in v0.1
docs.text:
Additional smartcore algorithms planned as potential follow-ups (not in v0.1):

  • Multiclass logistic regression
  • Regularized linear regression: Ridge, Lasso, ElasticNet
  • Decision trees and random forests
  • k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN)
  • Support Vector Machines (SVM)
  • Naive Bayes

docs.title: std/validate.tabular
docs.text:
Tabular data validation block with a built-in quality gate. Checks a Parquet dataset against declared schema, row-count, and per-column expectations before it reaches preprocessing or training. Behind the optional validate Cargo feature of mallops-std (not in default, no new crate dependency; enabled in mallops-cli). See SPEC FR-PRE-4.

blocks:
  validate:
    use: std/validate.tabular
    in: { data: raw.dataset }
    with:
      schema:
        - { name: age, type: int64 }
        - { name: income, type: float64 }
        - { name: plan, type: string }
        - { name: churned, type: bool }
        - { name: customer_id, type: int64 }
      allow_extra_columns: false
      min_rows: 100
      checks:
        age:
          max_null_fraction: 0.05
          min: 18
          max: 120
        income:
          max_null_fraction: 0.10
          min: 0.0
        plan:
          allowed: ["free", "pro", "enterprise"]
        customer_id:
          unique: true
      on_fail: fail

To skip downstream nodes instead of failing the run when validation fails:

blocks:
  validate:
    use: std/validate.tabular
    in: { data: raw.dataset }
    with:
      min_rows: 100
      checks:
        churned:
          max_null_fraction: 0.0
      on_fail: skip

docs.title: Configuration (with:)
docs.text:
Unknown fields are rejected (deny_unknown_fields). validate_config uses the same parser as run, so mallops validate catches configuration errors before execution.

Field Type Default Meaning schema list of { name, type } none Expected columns and their Arrow types (bool | int64 | float64 | string | date32). allow_extra_columns bool true Whether columns present in the dataset but not listed in schema are allowed. Requires schema: false without a schema is rejected (Error::Config). min_rows non-negative integer none Minimum number of rows required in the dataset (rows >= min_rows). checks map <column> → object none Per-column data quality expectations (see below). on_fail fail | skip fail Action when one or more checks fail. Note: unlike std/evaluate (where the default is skip), std/validate.tabular defaults to fail.

docs.title: checks.<column> fields
docs.text:
Key Type Constraints max_null_fraction f64 Finite value in [0.0, 1.0]. Passes iff null_count / row_count <= max_null_fraction. min f64 Finite inclusive lower bound (value >= min) for numeric columns (int64, float64). max f64 Finite inclusive upper bound (value <= max) for numeric columns (int64, float64). allowed list of JSON scalars Set of permitted non-null values. Supported only on string, int64, and bool columns. unique bool When true, all non-null values in the column must be distinct (supported on string, int64, float64, bool, date32; -0.0 equals 0.0 and all NaN are one value). unique: false is not an active check.

Validation rules (validate_config):

  • Unknown fields anywhere in with: are rejected (deny_unknown_fields).
  • min > max on the same column is rejected.
  • max_null_fraction outside [0.0, 1.0] or non-finite (NaN, ±inf) is rejected.
  • Non-finite min or max values (NaN, ±inf) are rejected.
  • A checks.<column> object needs at least one active check: {} and { unique: false } alone are rejected (unique: false next to another check is accepted).
  • allow_extra_columns: false without a schema is rejected.
  • allowed must be a non-empty list of strings, integers or booleans (floats, null, objects, [] are rejected).
  • Strings containing ${secret: anywhere in the config are rejected (as in std/external and std/evaluate).

docs.title: Ports
docs.text:
version: "0.1.0", Stage::Preprocess:

  • Block ID: std/validate.tabular
  • Input:
  • data (required): kind: dataset, format: parquet.
  • Outputs:
  • data: kind: dataset, format: parquet — carries the exact same payload and manifest content as the input data, but receives a new ArtifactId because the runtime sets manifest.parents to the input ArtifactId on commit (ADR-0007 D3).
  • report: kind: metrics, format: json — validation report written to report.json.

docs.title: Execution and check semantics
docs.text:
• Data problems are failed checks, not errors: any mismatch between the dataset and the configured expectations produces a failed check entry in report.json rather than aborting with Error::Runtime. This includes:
  • a column declared in schema or referenced in checks that is missing from the dataset;
  • a column whose Arrow type does not match the type declared in schema;
  • extra columns present when allow_extra_columns: false;
  • min or max configured on a non-numeric column;
  • allowed configured on a float64 (or other unsupported) column.
  • Exhaustive evaluation: all configured checks are evaluated on the dataset; validation does not stop at the first failure.
  • Null values: nulls count only toward max_null_fraction. Nulls are ignored by min, max, allowed, and unique.
  • Empty dataset (0 rows): the observed null fraction is 0.0 (so max_null_fraction passes). min and max pass on an empty dataset; min_rows fails if min_rows > 0.
  • All-null columns: min and max pass when every value in the column is null.
  • NaN values: NaN always fails min and max checks (same rule as std/evaluate).
  • allowed types: allowed is valid only on string, int64, and bool columns. Applying allowed to a float64 (or date32) column records a failed check.
  • In-memory loading: the entire input Parquet file is loaded into memory via the shared ingest Parquet reader.

docs.title: Output (report.json)
docs.text:
The report artifact payload is a single file, report.json, with a fixed, deterministic schema and check ordering:

{
  "v": 1,
  "passed": false,
  "checks": [
    {
      "check": "schema",
      "passed": false,
      "observed": {
        "missing": ["plan"],
        "mismatched": [{ "column": "age", "found": "float64" }],
        "extra": []
      },
      "expected": [
        { "name": "age", "type": "int64" },
        { "name": "plan", "type": "string" }
      ]
    },
    {
      "check": "min_rows",
      "passed": true,
      "observed": 250,
      "expected": 100
    },
    {
      "check": "min",
      "column": "age",
      "passed": false,
      "observed": 12,
      "expected": 18
    },
    {
      "check": "allowed",
      "column": "plan",
      "passed": false,
      "observed": { "count": 2, "examples": ["legacy", "trial"] },
      "expected": ["free", "pro", "enterprise"]
    }
  ]
}
  • v: report schema version, always 1.
  • passed: true iff every entry in checks has passed: true.
  • checks: array of { "check", "column"?, "passed", "observed", "expected" } in a fixed deterministic order:
  • a single schema check (no column): observed is { missing, mismatched, extra } (column names in schema order; mismatched entries are { column, found }; extra is listed only when allow_extra_columns: false), expected is the schema list. Type names are those of with.schema (int64, string, ...),
  • min_rows,
  • per-column checks, with columns sorted alphabetically and, within a column, in the fixed order max_null_fraction, min, max, allowed, unique.
  • Non-finite floats: NaN, +inf, and -inf are serialized as JSON strings "NaN", "inf", and "-inf" so report.json is always valid JSON.
  • observed for allowed and unique: { "count", "examples" } with at most 5 distinct offending values in ascending order. For allowed, count is the number of rows with a disallowed value and expected is the allowed list. For unique, count is the number of occurrences beyond the first of a repeated value and expected is { "count": 0 }.
  • observed for min / max: the observed minimum / maximum (null for an empty or all-null column, "NaN" if the column holds a NaN); for a non-numeric column, a text naming the type. observed is "missing column" when the column does not exist.
  • Manifest: the report manifest carries metadata.passed (bool), mirroring the report's passed.
  • No timestamps, run IDs, or block-written parents (the runtime injects parents on commit).

docs.title: Quality gate semantics (on_fail)
docs.text:
• All checks passed (passed == true): returns BlockOutcome::Produced with both data and report.
  • One or more checks failed with on_fail: fail (default):
  • Returns Error::Validation with one ValidationError per failed check; the single schema check yields one item per offending column (schema.<col>: missing column, unexpected type <type>, unexpected column).
  • Messages never contain data values: only check failed or <n> violating row(s) (allowed, unique).
  • The error paths (schema.<col>, min_rows, checks.<col>.<check>) refer to the validation report, not to the YAML pipeline definition.
  • The runtime marks the node Failed, cancels all descendants, does not commit data or report, leaves runs/latest.json unchanged, and mallops run exits 1.
  • One or more checks failed with on_fail: skip:
  • Returns BlockOutcome::Skipped (committing report so the failed report can be inspected) with reason validation failed: <path>, <path>, ... (the same paths as the fail errors).
  • Downstream blocking: the runtime skips downstream nodes that consume validate.data (or validate.report) as a required input. report reaches only downstream nodes that wire it as an optional input.
  • runs/latest.json and exit code: when any node is Skipped (and no node failed), mallops run leaves runs/latest.json unchanged and exits 0.
  • Caching: Skipped nodes are never cached by the runtime, so a failed validation is re-evaluated on the next run.

docs.title: Cache
docs.text:
CachePolicy::Deterministic { extra_hash: None }.

  • Same input data, config, node seed:, and block version hit the cache when the previous run Succeeded. Skipped and Failed runs are never cached.
  • Changing check semantics or report format requires bumping BlockSpec.version.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Situation Error Unknown field, min > max, max_null_fraction outside [0.0, 1.0] or non-finite, non-finite min/max, checks.<col> without an active check, allowed empty or with non-string/int64/bool items, allow_extra_columns: false without schema, ${secret: in config Error::Config (in mallops validate, aggregated into Error::Validation under blocks.<id>.with) One or more data checks failed with on_fail: fail Error::Validation (one item per failed check, per offending column for schema; report paths schema.<col>, min_rows, checks.<col>.<check>) Unreadable or corrupted input Parquet file Error::Runtime Cancellation via ctx.cancel() Error::Cancelled

Missing columns, type mismatches, min/max on non-numeric columns, and allowed on float64 are failed checks (handled by the on_fail gate), not Error::Runtime.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• In-memory dataset: the entire input Parquet file is loaded into memory. Streaming / out-of-core validation is planned for v0.2 (SPEC NFR-8).
  • No statistical drift detection in v0.1: comparing distributions across datasets (PSI, KS test) is planned for v0.3 (SPEC FR-MON-3).
